reviews.text: Beautiful

reviews.text: This review is primarily in regards to the head of security, George. We had an incident while visiting the property, and instead of trying to assist us, George was rude, dismissive, and petty. As a luxury property, people spend good money to stay, play and eat here. We simply asked for some help, and instead of helping us we were treated rudely. He refused to give his name or information, which tells you all you need to know- he knew he was wrong and didn’t want to be identified. I was able to get his name from the manager on duty. We are Hilton diamond lifetime members, and in all our years of traveling, we have never encountered anyone at any property as rude as George. Definitely made our decision to be loyal to the Hilton brand over the Marriott brand much easier.
reviews.author: L

reviews.text:
OMG breathtaking!

The whole hotel gives such luxury vintage vibes mixed with elegance and relaxation. The moment you walk in, everything feels so peaceful, classy, and aesthetic. The architecture and interior were absolutely beautiful definitely picture perfect everywhere 📸✨

And the spa experience!! Absolutely exceptional. The massage was honestly one of the BEST massage experiences I’ve ever had. So relaxing, calming, and refreshing. I left feeling like a whole new person 😭✨ The staff were also super professional, sweet, and welcoming the entire time.

The hotel itself was very clean, comfortable, and well maintained. Everything about this place felt luxurious and relaxing.

The scenery and atmosphere around the resort were also stunning. Such a perfect getaway spot if you want to relax, recharge, and treat yourself.

1000% recommend if you love elegant hotels, spa days, relaxing vibes, and aesthetic luxury experiences 💆‍♀️✨
reviews.author: Hiba Khan

reviews.text: I cannot remember visiting a better hotel than this. It’s classy once you walk in. Definitely high price but everything pretty much needs expectations. The food at all the restaurants was good. The little market for breakfast coffee has great breakfast sandwiches and breakfast burritos much better than Starbucks. Do not go to Starbucks just go to the breakfast market. The pool is great all the servers down at the pools are great. Never had an issue. Normally when you go to a hotel, there’s something that annoys you but here really nothing.

Staff are lazy. Managers lack discipline. Room service takes 2 hours to deliver food and it’s not good and taste like McDonalds cheap.

reviews.text: Got a resort pass for the day. Pool was nice and the food and drinks were good. My server was good. What wasn’t good was how absolutely rude the blonde bartender was, I have never been treated like that by someone in customer service probably ever. It was making me and everyone at the bar uncomfortable. I’d never come back here she ruined the whole experience honestly
reviews.author: Blake

reviews.text:
Our family’s experience at The Phoenician was incredibly disappointing and frankly unacceptable. During our stay, our children became seriously ill with food poisoning after eating at the resort, leading to multiple trips to the Emergency Room Well, on vacation in an unfamiliar area.

What made an already terrible situation even worse was how the resort chose to handle it. Instead of taking direct accountability or working with us in good faith to resolve such a serious matter, The Phoenician immediately pushed everything off onto their insurance company. This felt less like an effort to help and more like an attempt to shield themselves from responsibility while allowing the insurance provider to play the “bad guy” by denying our claim.

Now, because of that denial, we are left facing substantial medical bills, while our regular health insurance will not cover many of the costs. Rather than standing behind their guests after a serious incident, the resort’s approach appeared designed to distance itself from responsibility and avoid owning what happened.

For a property that prides itself on luxury and service, this lack of accountability was shocking. When your children’s health is impacted, you expect compassion, responsibility, and action—not corporate deflection. Our experience left us feeling abandoned, frustrated, and deeply let down.
reviews.author: A Weil

reviews.text: Gennaro, best host at the pool
reviews.author: Omar Al-Hayderi

reviews.text: Beautiful as always, since Charles Keating.
reviews.author: Nicholas Pela

reviews.text:
We had the pleasure of staying at the The Phoenician last month and thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

The resort itself is aesthetically beautiful, with an impressive range of activities and spaces for both families and adults. Multiple pools, several restaurants, recreational options, and quiet nooks throughout the property make it a destination where nearly everyone can find a place to relax.

What stood out most, however, was the service, particularly at check-in. Christian noticed that we shared a somewhat uncommon last name and took a few extra moments to genuinely get to know us. He made the arrival process effortless, but what happened later truly surprised us. When we returned to our room that evening, we found a heartfelt handwritten welcome note along with special snacks and a thoughtfully prepared margarita cocktail ensemble.

That level of personalization is increasingly rare today, especially in an era where staffing shortages often leave guests feeling rushed through transactional interactions. Experiences like this are a reminder that service is personal and meaningful, and that organizations capable of delivering it consistently likely invest well in their people and culture.

The rooms were well-appointed, the beds comfortable, and the bathrooms spacious and functional. As someone who admittedly notices details like water pressure, I can report that it was more than adequate. The on-site restaurants offered a nice variety of options, and the servers throughout the resort clearly understood what genuine hospitality looks like. The Tavern in particular was lively and enjoyable, with good live music and excellent service.

A couple of practical notes for future guests: reservations are highly recommended for the restaurants. The seating process can feel a bit cumbersome, with multiple hand-offs even during slower periods. Additionally, poolside service could be more attentive at times, as we occasionally needed to flag staff down.

That said, those issues were minor compared to the overall experience. While five stars may feel slightly generous given the price point and a few operational inefficiencies, on a 1–10 scale this resort is a very solid 9/10 and absolutely worthy of consideration for anyone visiting Scottsdale.
reviews.author: Richard Campagna

reviews.text:
Nice hotel and grounds. That's not why my stay was exceptional, however.

Many hotels today advertise themselves as five stars and under deliver.

reviews.text:
The staff were lovely, the grounds are pretty, but the hotel needs more TLC.

Specifically, my room was infested with ants and also had some small flying bugs- and I saw that many reviewers reported the same.

I reported this after leaving the hotel (I probably should have done so earlier) - I left a night early due to this.

I was very unimpressed by how their staff handled this when I emailed them about this after leaving.

I also had a very hard time getting through to the front desk or concierge for any requests - their line was always busy.
reviews.author: Samuel Eisenberg

reviews.text: The resort is looking very rundown and dated. Front desk didn't recognize Marriott status at all. Took 3 tries to get a room that was decent and then it still faced the lobby parking so was noisy and had zero view. First room smelled like sewer - so bad you could smell it in the hallway. 2nd room's balcony literally faced a wall. Everything was extremely overpriced - $28 for an espresso martini! Cold shower in spa didn't work and didn't have instructions on how to use. Spa services were great but very pricey - especially with the 22% required gratuity added. Food was decent but very overpriced. The tea was nice but the food was just ok. Room service delivery person was very friendly and helpful, food was hot and tasty. Pool was surprisingly a little chilly and our reserved chaise lounges were at the family pool when we had requested the adult pool. First impression was that this would be a fun place to come with friends (I was with my adult daughter on this trip). But after seeing the clientele and the prices I don't think I would return. I would try a different place in Scottsdale - though maybe Scottsdale isn't my scene.
reviews.author: Debbie Way

reviews.text: Things have changed in this community since the pandemic. It is on a downward spiral! Not what it used to be the staff has also changed and management is unresponsive.
reviews.author: Ms.Theresa Stewart-Bouhdida M.Ed.

reviews.text: We didn't stay on site, but we brought our group here for a pickleball networking event and it was an absolute hit! Missy and Chef Nick went above and beyond to create a menu that perfectly fit our group’s needs. I had unfortunately missed a deadline, which made things tricky, but Chef Nick somehow pulled everything together flawlessly—and it ended up being exactly what we wanted. On the courts, Dan and Ivan were incredible. They coached our guests, kept everything organized, and ran the tournament so smoothly. Everyone had an amazing time! This was our first time doing an activity like this, but it’s safe to say it will be part of our regular rotation. Thank you all for such a fantastic experience!

reviews.text: Spent 9 days and the highlight was the exceptional service from the staff. The ballrooms are excellent and the banquet staff is on point. They never missed a beat and even helped us with moving signage around the resort. The resort is beautiful although some of the rooms could use updating. Camelback mountain as the backdrop makes it for a spectacular view. I was thoroughly impressed with my stay. Thank you!
reviews.author: Jonathan Soave

reviews.text: Stayed here for a work trip . Although the resort was comfortable and beautiful , we were charged random different amounts to our credit card every single day. When leaving I was told that my room charges were a total of $87 US which they had also provided me a bill for the night before . Since we have been home ( for almost a month ) I still have 3 charges unaccounted for , have called them numerous times and I’m assured that these charges will be returned and they haven’t been. It doesn’t even make sense to have more than one room charge after a week stay? I would expect that after calling more than once to rectify the charges I would have received a call with at least an explanation of the charges . I believe this was a mix up with how our work team set up payments for breakfasts ( using coupons ) and staff accidentally charging it to my room. BE WARNED !

reviews.author: elizabeth park

reviews.text:
Anniversary Trip
For years, we’ve been intending to go to The Phoenician when we had an opportunity to celebrate and so we decided to go on our 32nd wedding anniversary. Upon arrival, the staff was certainly nice but seemed like there weren’t enough of them. After flying from the East Coast and a pretty long travel day, I think there were four people in line to be checked in and only one of the six registration desk in operation. We did not arrive at a weird time. It was in the middle of the afternoon about the time check-in’s were starting. Our room was as expected very nice, clean pretty contemporary. The amenities in the bathroom were very nice. During our stay, we ate at multiple of the food outlets the pool bar and the fast casual alternative were unremarkable. Fine but not necessarily what you might expect at one of the nicer hotels. We did eat at the steakhouse and it was a fantastic experience. The service was what you would expect and the food was even better. Our primary purpose for this trip was just to enjoy the Scottsdale weather and sun and so the pool was the focus of our trip and we were very disappointed. We did not use the upper pool. It was mostly family oriented, and there seemed to be a lot going on and everybody having a good time, we focused on the adult pool and then what they call the mother of pearl Pool the mother pearl pool was all ages pool and early in the morning was very nice and mostly clean, we spent the bulk of our time at the adult pool, which was very lacking. The pool itself was very old and dated the tiles had a thick layer of scum on them and the pool felt just generally dirty. The water was cloudy and it seemed as though wasn’t being very well cared for. To be fair the pool deck service people did an excellent job keeping you hydrated offering new fresh towels, willingness to help you move your chairs and keep yourself covered under umbrellas. It was more of facilities problem than a service problem. If you were going to this hotel for a pool experience, I would choose another. I cannot speak to the golf tennis and spa facilities. They all look very nice and people seem to be having a very good time but as for a pool trip, we were disappointed.
reviews.author: scott henegar

reviews.text: Our grand deluxe room looked out over a cement pad that had various conventions every night.  During the day it was like a construction zone - putting up tables, chairs- and in the evening it was like a frat party- loud music and conventioneers.  Very little luxury left in this old dame.  It’s a convention center.  If you’re not with the convention you would be a damn fool to stay here.  Avoid at all costs

reviews.text: Can’t put my finger on what it was exactly but something was off. We arrived and were able to check in and get into our room at 9:30am which was awesome! When we got there, there was a candy bar rapper, and some papers on the dresser. Later that night, when we went to use the bathtub, the drain did not work so water constantly drained out of the tub while you were in it. The worst part was the air conditioning was not working. It would get cold but then in the middle of the night AC would shut off and my husband and I would be sweating and have to take all the blankets off. This happened multiple times. The pool staff was awesome and the food by the pool was fantastic. However, the pools themselves did not feel very clean. There was so much hair at the bottom of the pool and my husband and I kept getting wads of hair stuck between our toes, they sell pool cleaners… those should be ran every single night. We had an extremely disappointing meal at the Mowrey restaurant. My husband‘s food was cold and the flavor was awful. We have been to some really nice resorts and hotels around the world. I guess with this being a five star resort and how much people love it I was expecting a little more attention to detail and cleanliness. There was a lot of wear and tear. You could tell around the doors and light switches and everything just needed a little facelift. For the price you pay I was very surprised by the way some of the main bathrooms looked. One of the sinks by the pool  was clogged the whole time and cloudy brown water was sitting in it. The doors looked like a campground site with raccoon claws trying to get out of the bathroom… it was interesting.

reviews.text: Valet blocked me from dropping off a guest. Then blocked again driving a white Toyota highlander when trying to leave, he honked at me as I drove by. Guest remarked how unprofessional they were. Will never recommend this establishment.
reviews.author: Chris Pasley

reviews.text:
We had a really enjoyable stay at The Phoenician overall, with several standout moments that made the experience memorable.

First, housekeeping was excellent—our room was consistently spotless, refreshed on time, and maintained to a high standard throughout our stay. That level of attention definitely added to the comfort and luxury feel of the resort.

A special thank you to Bradley at the concierge desk, who was absolutely fantastic—knowledgeable, attentive, and genuinely invested in making sure we had a great experience. Another concierge team member (I believe her name started with “S”) was also very helpful and pleasant, contributing to the overall great service we received in that area.

The only downside during our stay was an interaction with a young lady handling room service calls, which did not reflect the level of service expected at a resort of this caliber. However, we appreciated that the front desk manager addressed the concern promptly and professionally, restoring the level of service we anticipated.

Overall, a beautiful property with excellent service recovery and standout staff—would definitely return.
reviews.author: EDRICA RICHARDSON

reviews.text:
Our spring break at the Phoenician was nothing short of extraordinary—truly one of the most memorable family trips we’ve ever had. From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed with warmth, professionalism, and a level of care that made us feel completely at home.

A special thank you to Sherry at breakfast, who made every morning such a joy. She went above and beyond to make sure our kids were happy and well taken care of, always greeting us with a smile and remembering the little details that made our experience feel personal and special. Breakfast quickly became one of our favorite parts of the day because of her.

Price at the front desk was equally incredible. He made check-in seamless and set the tone for our stay with his friendly, attentive service. Anytime we had a question or needed assistance, he handled it with genuine kindness and efficiency. It’s clear he takes pride in creating a great guest experience.

And we absolutely cannot say enough about the staff at the hotel pools. They were phenomenal—always attentive, upbeat, and so patient with families. Whether it was helping us find the perfect spot, keeping things running smoothly, or just adding to the fun atmosphere, they made our pool days unforgettable for both us and our kids.

The entire property is stunning, the amenities are top-notch, and the service is consistently exceptional. What really sets the Phoenician apart, though, is the people. Every single staff member we encountered made us feel valued and cared for.

We left already talking about when we can come back. Thank you for an incredible spring break—we’ll be recommending this place to everyone we know!
reviews.author: Colleen Clarke

reviews.text:
We stayed here for our spring break, and it was truly one of the most amazing places we’ve ever experienced. From the moment we arrived, everything felt top-notch—this is a true five-star resort in every sense. The property is absolutely stunning, with beautifully maintained grounds, luxurious amenities, and an atmosphere that perfectly blends elegance with relaxation. Every detail—from the rooms to the service—was impeccable.
I can’t say enough good things about our stay. This is easily one of the most beautiful Marriott properties we’ve visited, and we would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a memorable, upscale getaway. We can’t wait to come back!
reviews.author: Arteida Bickford

reviews.text: We had a poor experience checking in but I have to say the manager whose name is Price went above and beyond to make things up to us. He was a gentleman and he is the reason I would come back. He’s a true professional and did a great job with us.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Denha

reviews.text:
Nothing about this hotel is luxury. 4 star at best. We arrived to our interconnecting rooms and walked straight back out. In what can only be compared to a motel block, the carpet was taped down with black masking tape, stains over furniture, general signs of years of wear and tear were hugely obvious. Even our balcony had some sort of juice stain that hadn’t been cleaned from the previous guests. We went back to reception to tell them we were changing hotels when they suddenly found us interconnecting rooms in the main hotel (previously unavailable). Whilst still a far stretch from what we would consider luxury - especially for close to $1000 per night per room - these were better than our previous option. Douglas agreed to modify the rate too - thank goodness because we’d have been sick paying what we’d originally committed to.

However the disappointment didn’t end there. Discarded glasses and rubbish decorate communal areas. Staircases and outdoor areas haven’t had a thorough sweep or wipe down for what looks like months. Pool loungers are very uncomfortable with thin basic towels. There is a queue for breakfast everyday and you’re unable to make reservations. Free coffee machines and milk canisters are often found empty. Asked for an ice coffee at the pool but apparently this isn’t on offer and I have to go into one of the restaurants to see if they might serve it - this would be totally acceptable for a hotel that doesn’t claim to be 5 star luxury.

Staff are friendly enough, but most don’t go over and above. I can only assume lacking a manager who is experienced in what 5 star luxury actually means. It appears other recent reviews emulate our experience and I only wish we had studied these before making our reservation.

Kids were happy enough with tennis and pool areas. But unless this hotel has a huge overhaul, its increasingly negative reputation will get the better of it.
reviews.author: Amy Windmill

reviews.text: A great place to enjoy
reviews.author: Mr.Chris SD

reviews.text: We booked an Easter Brunch @ J&G steakhouse because they told us we could participate in Easter activities. My 9 yr old was very excited only to tell us that it was for hotel guests only, so we won’t be coming back here. Thanks for ruining my son’s Easter.
reviews.author: luviminda Garcia

reviews.text: This place was pretty nice, but it's a little too fancy for me. The pools were too cold to go in, but the food was pretty good. The lighting and the mountain at night were gorgeous! We ended up switching to the JW Marriott after one night.
reviews.author: Dustin LaFavre

reviews.text:
My husband and I chose The Phoenician for a mini-honeymoon, using a large number of Marriott points with the expectation of an exceptional, elevated experience. Based on its “luxury” branding and AAA Five Diamond status, we arrived genuinely excited. Unfortunately, that excitement quickly turned into confusion and disappointment.

I’m still struggling to understand how this property maintains a 4-star rating. The gap between what was advertised and what was delivered was…impressive.

The room itself was perfectly average. Not offensive, but not memorable either. If someone told me it was a standard 2 or 3 star hotel room, I wouldn’t question it. The balcony was nice, but certainly not enough to justify the “luxury” label.

Where things really fell apart though was the service.

Standard housekeeping was not provided. Over a 6-day stay, despite calling and even going to the front desk in person, we never received a proper room cleaning. At one point, someone stopped by, made the bed, and dropped off towels…while leaving behind dirty wine glasses and trash. An interesting interpretation of “service.” It gets better. Later that same day, a bottle of champagne and fruit were delivered as a congratulatory honeymoon gift (a thoughtful gesture). However, it was placed right alongside the same uncollected garbage, which made the experience feel more way more awkward than celebratory.

Fast forward to when we eventually ran out of toilet paper, we had to walk to the front desk to ask for more. At that point, it genuinely felt like we might as well have packed our own. What stood out most wasn’t just the inconvenience—it was how completely unfazed the staff seemed and how they handled it - with lack of urgency or apology.

At the pool, we ordered hummus that took an hour to arrive. After asking a waitress, it was pretty clear the order had been forgotten. Again, things happen—but the food finally arrived undercooked and underwhelming.

Ironically, the only smooth experiences we had were the ones we paid extra for—like the $450 cabana. And to be fair, the golf cart staff were excellent and easily the highlight of the service we encountered.

Thankfully, we spent much of our time off-property hiking and kayaking, which ended up being the best part of the trip, likely because it meant less time dealing with the hotel.

I don’t typically write reviews, but this experience was too disappointing to ignore. When you market yourself as a luxury property, the expectation isn’t perfection—it’s basic hospitality paired with elevated service. Unfortunately, this stay delivered neither.

The worst part about this entire experience has actually been having to relive it by writing this review. But my intention is to save others from having to go through a similar experience.
reviews.author: G Englehart

reviews.text:
Devon the concierge was incredible.
Everything about this place was truly enchanting, from the staff- making it their business to meet everyone’s needs, to the tranquil spa, and the outdoor pool attendants; this resort is truly a retreat space that must be be missed!
reviews.author: Dr. Sharon Fried-Buchalter

The service was impeccable and we were never wondering where our attendant Raymond was, as he was always available to order drinks or food. The pool was very nice and never seemed crowded although there was quite a number of other family’s there also.
reviews.author: Tim Callahan

reviews.text: We rented cabana for the day. It was the luxury you want and expect
reviews.author: Kristy Callahan

reviews.text: Fantastic place! Love the location and the service! The staff is great, rooms are spacious, and the pool is amazing.
reviews.author: Brian Drewes

reviews.text: Great place everyone  should go there
reviews.author: Jerry Leon

reviews.text:
We had an absolutely incredible experience at The Phoenician—truly a five-star stay from start to finish.

A very special thank you to Allie, Lolita, Emma, and Cameo, who supported us through every phase of planning—from months before our arrival all the way through departure. Coordinating a group trip of 45 people is no small undertaking, and their attention to detail, responsiveness, and professionalism ensured everything went off without a hitch. They genuinely went above and beyond in every possible way.

The property itself is stunning, and the level of service is truly next-level across the board.

We’d also like to recognize Max, who did an outstanding job organizing a large group of us for a Saturday morning golf outing, making the experience seamless and enjoyable for everyone. Erica was equally fantastic in arranging our cabana rentals—thanks to her thoughtful planning and recommendations, we had an unforgettable pool party day that our entire group is still talking about.

Overall, this was one of the best group travel experiences we’ve ever had. Every single person in our group loved the resort, and we are so grateful to the entire team at The Phoenician for making it so memorable. We cannot wait to return!
reviews.author: Kelly Lee

reviews.text: Despite being an older resort, the rooms and resort in general is updated. Very clean inside the rooms with comfortable bedding. The shower products and added amenities came in handy. The pools were clean and open 24hr. Temperature was comfortable and required minimal adjustments. Kid friendly resort with many things to do. Highly recommend as a quiet and quick get away!
reviews.author: Lori Garcia

reviews.text:
Friendly staff, incredible views, plenty to do. We ate at every restaurant and market they had, it was all good. You could come and never leave the resort really.
There’s a hike within walking distance, Camels-back that allows a panoramic view of the city. The rooms were immaculate, the spa did wonderful work and overall we had a lovely stay here. There’s pools, tennis courts, an athletic center, golf course, pickleball courts, a waterslide and many options for lodging.
reviews.author: Nykol Bailey Rice

reviews.text: Great stay here. Good food at lunch spot by pools, the 3 pools were great. Great service from valet, check in, staff by pool. Would Recommend! beautiful mountain views from the pool.
reviews.author: Matt Painter

reviews.text: Very beautiful hotel with incredible desert scenery. The territory is large and well maintained. Staff were polite and helpful. It feels peaceful and luxurious at the same time. I really enjoyed staying here. Spoiling my self for International Womans Day! Would love to come back. And love the new portable chargers available at the pool since we forgot ours at home.
reviews.author: Genie Poliak

reviews.text:
I recently stayed at the hotel and had a really positive experience. From the moment I arrived, check-in was smooth and welcoming.

What stood out most during my stay was Sara, who took care of my room. She came twice a day and did an exceptional job. She was incredibly kind, organized, and thoughtful. She didn’t just clean the room - she paid attention to the little things. She neatly organized my belongings, kept everything spotless, and was very respectful of my space. I noticed that she would wait until I stepped out before coming in to service the room, which I really appreciated. Her professionalism and warmth made a real impression on me and made the stay feel comfortable and cared for.

I also ordered breakfast both mornings I was there, and Jordyn was fantastic. She was courteous, friendly, and very respectful. She set everything up nicely and made sure I had everything I needed. It’s the kind of service that feels genuine and welcoming, and it started my mornings on a great note.

The property itself is beautiful. There are plenty of outdoor seating areas where you can relax and enjoy the surroundings. The atmosphere feels open, calm, and well maintained.
reviews.author: Aneesa M.

reviews.text: Beautiful location in the heart of paradise valley. Stunning hotel and nice well maintained quiet pool areas. We got a cabana and the space and amenities were amazing. The service from Victor was top notch. The food and drinks were also excellent. Loved the nutty maitai and the kebabs. Highly recommend for a fancy, relaxing pool day.
reviews.author: Bridgid Conn

reviews.text: Have been staying here for over 20 years, This is our go to place to stay. Rooms are clean, Staff is friendly and helpful, food offering is great, Amenities are awesome, and the golf course is great!
reviews.author: Lml Lml

reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here and loved it! The entire resort is a dream- from the main lobby, to the rooms to the beautiful pools!
reviews.author: Tiffany Pershall

reviews.text: The Phoenician, a Luxury Collection Resort, Scottsdale has jaw-dropping desert views, lush grounds, and picture-perfect pools. 🌴💦 But the charm fades fast: rooms feel dated in spots, service is inconsistent, and on-site dining is overpriced. 💸 Pools get crowded, and the resort vibe leans more “polished showroom” than relaxing escape. Gorgeous for photos, but the full luxury experience doesn’t quite deliver. 📸⚠️
reviews.author: The Real Travel Edit

reviews.text: Very nice hotel. Huge property really no need to even leave the resort.
reviews.author: Reva Dallo

reviews.text: We have been coming here for years. We will never come here again. Paying over $1k per night and willing to pay for a suite, we dealt with endless holds on the front desk, broken promises for things like a break down of the couch bed, foam pillows, etc. We sat in the bar for an hour without service. Normally benign stuff but not when you are paying this much for a room. Do not stay here, it is ridiculously below standard.
reviews.author: Eric Rossman

reviews.text: The hotel is showing it's age; however, the service was great. The location is great; we had a mountain view room. We spent several different times at the pool and the staff were great.
reviews.author: Bob Parker

reviews.text: Beautiful resort... All the staff we interacted with were great, some Id even call excellent. Good food at all the on property restaurants. Try the wings at the lobby bar! Good conference facilities.
reviews.author: Travis Broadwater

reviews.text: 3 stars because the spa would not return a phone call, email or inhouse communication when trying to schedule an appointment, even a month ahead of time. After all this is supposed to be a resort and place for relaxation.

reviews.text: Rachel at the front desk is amazing

reviews.text: Beautiful property, well maintained and very courteous staff.
reviews.author: Zach Newman

reviews.text:
For price it is shocking the condition of the accommodations. Furniture stained, bathroom door doesn’t close, outlets not properly secured to wall, bathroom faucets not attached property, and I could go on.

I strongly recommend choosing another option.
reviews.author: Ryan Liscom

reviews.text:
Fantastic location with beautiful views of Camelback Mountain. That said, for the price point, I expected more elevated amenities. We were disappointed to learn that the spa no longer offers day passes since COVID and that they haven’t been brought back.

I visited with my husband while he was attending a conference, and the conference events and meals I joined him for were truly spectacular. Overall, this is a great option if you’re considering The Phoenician for an organization’s conference or event.
reviews.author: Meggie Hoerr

reviews.text: I’ve stayed here a few times. World class resort with world class amenities and offerings. Absolutely beautiful hotel carved into the base of camelback mountain. You’d be hard pressed to find a better resort in this region.
reviews.author: Todd Locker

reviews.text: My daughter booked the tea experience for 9 people for her 30th birthday and got sick. She tried to cancel or reschedule 24 hrs before but was told she had no options.  They don't care. Now she's out $315! Would not recommend.
reviews.author: Yvette

reviews.text: Extremely expensive food and drinks in bar. Music was great
reviews.author: Bill Danielson

reviews.text: I went there on new year's eve to meet a client and do some business. I hadn't been there in a few years.It's very nice, excellent place.I recommend staying there
reviews.author: Vern Gamble

reviews.text: Best resort in Phoenix
reviews.author: Rick Palumbo

reviews.text:
Lots to unpack here. The property itself is a gem. What a great retreat away from the city. Check in was easy and staff was attentive. Let me go category by category on my experiences.

Service team: generally excellent. Our dinner service at the steakhouse was exceptional and the staff there deserve tons of praise. The lobby shop staff was less than friendly - one woman there told several people they were separate from the hotel and couldn't do room charges ("well we could but it would be a pain"), which she said almost with some pride. The only thing she said to me was "we don't allow returns or exchanges" as if I might look like I was going to wear the clothes then return them when I was done. It was weird.

Food all over was excellent, to the pool cafe and the two restaurants we ate at. Breakfast was tiny, way overpriced and basic but that was a small hiccup - but don't expect any good espresso drinks here.

We stayed in a casita and it was a bit disappointing. The shower was super tiny - think airline economy bathroom - yet the giant bathtub took up literally 1/2 the bathroom proper. The shower head and hand sprayer both sprayed at the same time with no means to turn one off. The knob was broken. And, the door leaked with every shower so half our towels went straight to the floor. Our casita had a walk-out to the parking structure only, terrible view. With no kitchen, a micro fridge, no microwave, it felt like a much cheaper room. Bed was nice though!

The real disappointment for me was, there was really no "kid free" zone. There were two hot tubs lined with kids, even late at night. It's less like a resort and more like a kids water park. My towels were taken by others twice in 30 minutes, (once by staff and once by a child).

This place has potential and I wanted to like it. Even at our romantic, $600 dinner at the steakhouse we were surrounded by children! It kind of ruined the experience for us. The adults only pool was in the middle of the chaos and not peaceful at all. We won't be back unless they work to segregate these areas better. I think we learned our lesson.
reviews.author: T Esk

reviews.text: Do not stay here, and whatever you do, do not book a casita. They are like run down college dorm apartments. They moved us to the main tower but it still did not meet what we were expecting. There's another Marriott property at Camelback that has stunning casitas and rooms, highly recommend looking there. They think very highly of themselves here and it's not worth the price.
reviews.author: Jeff Ghirardo

reviews.text: Rooms very expensive: nearly $1K+ night 12/28-30/2025. Great location. Rooms are solid, though shower is a bit cramped.
reviews.author: Ben Slivka

reviews.text: Very dated rooms and hotel, broken water pipes lead to no running water/toilets for over 10-hours. We received no notifications or messages as to the water going out and no updates during the day. When we finally waited in line for over an hour at 10pm at night we were moved rooms wjth the promise not to have to move again, until the next day when we were moved again…terrible experience for a lux resort would never go back or recommend. Once moved to the canyon suites we enjoyed ourselves, but would not suggest the main hotel.
reviews.author: Brita Turner

reviews.text: Very conveniently placed, only 20 minutes from the airport, 10 minutes away from old town Scottsdale, and 10 minutes away from a gas station. The rooms were very large and had a great view of orchid falls we loved sitting outside near the fire place  because of the view. The restaurants had a very good view but there were limited options.
reviews.author: Ashwaray Chaba

reviews.text:
We had to wait close to 3 hours for our room.
The room is nice but it is not enjoyable sitting on the balcony since next to the pool in front of the balconies there is a large enclosure of the heating/air-conditioning commercial unit making significant noise.
reviews.author: Rupert A.

reviews.text: Gorgeous grounds. Beautiful rooms. Delicious food.
reviews.author: Kim

reviews.text:
Marriott elite member here. Came here for an early Xmas escape. I didn't book the room but as a Marriott member, this location is not a "luxury" resort as they brand themselves to be. On our last day, they had a water pipe burst and shut down all the water in the resort. We couldn't even use a restroom for about 5 hours until they brought porta jons to the front of the hotel to use. And then the staff offered a "free" bus to another hotel to shower. My guess is that when Marriott bought this property, they took a significant amount of risk on the infrastructure and a max capacity tested their limits.

On top of the water issues, the rooms are old and dated, adult pool is surrounded by kids pools and, and everything is overpriced just due to the Phoenician name and history of the resort. If you are a Marriott member I would recommend the W or JW Marriott over this property.
reviews.author: Randy Mulder

reviews.text:
The staff is fantastic, food is really solid.
The building, facilities, rooms are a little past due. Outdated in some spots, showing wear in others.

Gym is up to date, golf is great. But some maybe most rooms are subpar for the price. You could rent a home for the cost of staying here for twice the days & just pay to golf here instead.

I repeat the staff is fantastic but the great people can’t make up for the lack of investment in the property.
reviews.author: SJ Douglas

reviews.text: The Phoenician in Scottsdale offers an exceptional luxury experience. From the beautifully designed rooms to the attentive and friendly staff, every detail is carefully considered. The resort’s amenities, including the stunning pools, world-class dining, and serene spa, create the perfect blend of relaxation and indulgence. The location is ideal, with breathtaking desert views and easy access to local attractions. Every moment felt special, and the level of service made the stay unforgettable. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a luxurious getaway.
reviews.author: CC

reviews.text: Here luxury is everywhere, every single detail is made with a fine sense of beauty and style, I tried hard to find something that is average looking, there’s none! Place is huge but so well maintained, in other similar places you’d bump into maintenance and housekeeping people in every corner, but not here, wonder how they keep it glowing with almost zero disturbances. Moving to the outside, the Camelback mountain starts just outside my room, a huge mass of rocks and cactus climbing up into the blue sky. You have to go to the top, just make sure you bring a bottle of water because the air is dry. Watching the sunset from the top of the mountain is soul refreshing, and it’s not too late to go back before it gets dark, it should take about 30 minutes to go down the trail.

reviews.text:
Stayed here in November. I expected a true luxury experience, but unfortunately, the visit fell far short of that promise. For a resort that markets itself as one of Phoenix’s premier destinations, the overall stay was surprisingly underwhelming.

When we arrived, it was clear that the level of service did not match the resort’s reputation or price point. Staff felt inattentive at check in.

The room itself was also disappointing. It's a basic room that didn't feel luxurious at all. We had walls that had spilled liquid on the walls (see photo). While the property is visually nice, the accommodations didn’t reflect the same level of care. Certain amenities felt outdated, and cleanliness was no where near what it should have been.

For the cost and the reputation, I expected a significantly better stay. Unfortunate.

reviews.text: Q, Brad and the front desk team are absolutely Ah-May-Zing. Dani is my favorite bartender in the quiet lobby bar. The entire team repeatedly goes above and beyond to make us feel special and appreciated!

Theres a kids water park but you can get away from the noise. The pool chairs are plentiful but uncomfortable. reviews.text: Took my grandson for 18th birthday October 18-20. The young lady that checked us in was very professional and friendly. The gentleman who took our bags to room was very nice and professional and all the housekeeping staff.The lady who checked us out was very rude and bad attitude. Had stayed in Canyon Suites in January 2025 and everyone was very friendly and excellent customer service.In the future I would go back to Canyon Suites where there is stellar service.

reviews.text: Went to the Phoenician for afternoon tea. The service was exceptional,  the tea was good and the sandwiches, biscuits, and pastries were all very good. The view was awesome! I will make every effort to stay at the Hotel on my next trip to the Phoenix area.

reviews.text: We spent 4 nights here in late October 2025. The hotel is laid out on a large piece of land with plenty of space to wander. Our room was facing the cacti garden and was a quiet location. Even though we were on the fifth floor we could access the garden and walk through it to get to the lobby and other parts of the hotel. We had meetings here and utilized the meeting rooms and east and west lawns for breakfast and lunch. They had plenty of umbrellas to give shade during these meals. The food for all meals was a wide variety of options from protein, carbs and fruits.
reviews.author: Diane Williams

reviews.text: My husband and I absolutely love this resort. So much so we are on our 5th visit for my birthday and our Anniversary. We were married at the resort 2 years ago and we love it here. The staff are top notch and so attentive and the housekeeping staff is remarkable. I only have one complaint. We have been here 4 nights and it is usually a welcome get away. However, unfortunately we were here during a large conference of over 600 attendees who had a large and very loud outdoor breakfast starting at 7am right outside our window on every single morning we have been staying here. At 8am they call all attendees in with a loud bell from breakfast, so if the noise of 600 people didn't already wake you, the bell will. For a couple who were here for a birthday/anniversary trip on a break from children this was a bit disappointing. Next time you should place all of the conference attendees in the same area of the hotel that overlooks this very loud breakfast and put the rest of us who want to sleep in past 645am on the other side of the hotel.
reviews.author: Michelle Carlson

reviews.text: Beautiful resort. Modern look and feel. Great views of the city. Clean. Restaurants, shops & pools are all great. The falconier to help keep the birds away from the outdoor tables at the restaurant was a fun & unique feature.

reviews.text: I was really enjoy the night at Jokake, wonderful place, friendly service. Tin and Anthony is really friendly and helpful .
reviews.author: Harry

reviews.text:
If I had to sum up the Phoenician in a single sentence, I would say: it seems like a property that was once great, but has significantly lost its luster.

I’ll start with the good. Everyone working at the Phoenician that we interacted with was excellent, both genuinely friendly as well as very helpful and competent. The property itself and the grounds are beautiful, nestled into the foothills of Camelback Mountain. The spa services were fantastic, and the restaurants were very good.

Now here’s the cons. This feels like a resort that has about 300 fewer people working there than it should. For just an example, something simple like a request for ice to our room required nearly an hour wait and a follow up phone call. This doesn’t seem like anyone not doing their job appropriately, but simply that there wasn’t enough people for the requests that were made. For another, at their marketplace, on a weekday, with a conference going on, it seemed like there was only one, very kind, but very stressed out guy working at the counter (making food, coffee, taking orders, etc). This was a frequent experience/thought I had during our stay.

At the pools, what should have been a polished experience, given the location, was lackluster. The pools were freezing cold, to the extent that almost no one except for some brave children were using them. Are their heaters not being maintained? Or turned off to save cost? The pool chairs at this luxury property were mostly basic pool chairs and the tables for drinks were wicker and falling apart. Our server on several days, was very nice, but seemingly was attending to three different levels of pools, meaning we were often waiting for extended periods of time to order another drink, food, or get our tab (not for lack of her effort, to be clear). The pool experience at a luxury property should be a luxury experience, fast service, towel service, heated pools, comfortable chairs. This felt like a pool at a low end all inclusive (without the free drinks).

Finally the rooms. Remember, this is a property that often charges $900+ a night, if not more. We were in the casitas, and upon arriving, the outdoor firepit was out of propane, and our in room phone didn’t work. The temperature control was lackluster, needing to be kept at 65 degrees to maintain a comfortable air temp, and even then the vents was dripping onto the floor (and the covered in dust). Our one experience with in room dining was good, but the pickup took nearly two hours, with the person knocking on our door at nearly 10 PM. At one point in the bathroom we also found a large spider web hanging from the ceiling. Again, at a lower caliber property, all these things are to be expected. At a five star resort in Marriott’s luxury line? This is unacceptable.

All in all, my experience was fine, to pretty good. Obviously all these issues are minor. Unfortunately, because of the cost, these seemingly minor issues leave a poor taste in your mouth. For my money, next time I’ll go with a Ritz Carlton or Four Seasons, which seems to be much more reliable in their attention to detail and understanding real high level service and experience.
reviews.author: Matthew Hanrahan

reviews.text:
I’m not a person who carry’s cash but it eventually ran out of cash to tip valet and boy that little man who help load our car gave My colleague and I the worst attitude ever. I only stayed one night and just do happened to have two $20 bills. Anywho that money was gone the same day as check in.

This stay was meant to be a wellness stay before going back to work. There was no immediate need to leave the hotel. Late check out was also complimentary. My room was spacious, bedding was nice, my bathroom was aesthetically pleasing. The best part about the room was the double doors to the patio to take in the fresh air and view the mountains. I would definitely stay here again.
reviews.author: Mary B

reviews.text:
Not worth the money, not even close. We paid around $1,000 a night with all the hidden fees (and that’s after discounts), and this place simply isn’t worth more than $300 a night all in.
Prices are outrageous, and it feels like they’re trying to squeeze every dollar out of you at every step.

Yes, the hotel and pools are nice, but you’ll find similar pools and comfort at much cheaper hotels nearby. Nothing here truly justifies the insane prices except maybe the view, and even that’s not worth paying such an absurd premium for.

Self-parking far from the rooms is $30 a day, faster Wi-Fi costs extra, and you constantly get the sense that everything has an added charge. It’s a beautiful property ruined by greed.

Bottom line: you can easily find a $200–300 hotel in Scottsdale that will give you an equal or even better experience without draining your wallet.
reviews.author: Rubi Baruch

reviews.text:
Where do I even start?! From the moment we arrived, The Phoenician delivered an unforgettable experience of luxury, ease, and pure indulgence. Every single detail... from the breathtaking views of Camelback Mountain to the impeccably designed rooms... made this birthday getaway feel like a true oasis in the desert.

The property itself is immaculate; modern elegance with a classic touch. The grounds are perfectly maintained, the pools are serene and photo-worthy, and the spa? Absolutely divine. I spent hours unwinding at the rooftop spa pool, and I can honestly say I left floating.

But what really made this stay exceptional was the service. Every staff member we encountered was warm, attentive, and genuinely helpful...from valet to concierge to the poolside attendants. They didn’t just meet expectations, they anticipated our needs. One staff member even gave us spot-on recommendations for local restaurants and lounges that ended up being highlights of our trip.

This hotel understands the meaning of true hospitality. Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion or just in need of a luxurious escape, The Phoenician will wrap you in comfort, class, and a kind of care that’s hard to put into words.

I can't wait to return. Consider this my official love letter to The Phoenician.
reviews.author: Ericka Elle

reviews.text: Fairly nice but a little rundown
reviews.author: Ted Becker

reviews.text: We visited the  Resort in mid-September, when daytime temperatures soared above 110°F in the area. The artificial turf around the pool intensified the heat, making the pools feel uninviting. The hotel itself was massive, lacking the intimate ambiance we hoped for, and instead felt overwhelming and oppressive. Unfortunately, several groups of very loud locals made it difficult to hold a conversation, and we ended up leaving the bar. On a positive note, the restaurant food was good, the cocktails were excellent, and the staff was friendly. Overall, however, the experience was not enjoyable.

reviews.text: Stayed at the Canyon Suites, which are phenomenal.  You get access to the Phoenician facilities.  Overall, it’s pretty good.  The pool food the first day was awesome.  Ordered the same thing the next, and found an unwelcomed surprise.  A piece of long metal wire in the green salsa.  I put it in my mouth but thankfully spit it out quickly.  The server took it back and didn’t charge, but no management acknowledgment or anything.  This could have been a very serious issue, which thankfully it wasn’t for all parties.  Staff needs trained for odd events like this.

reviews.text:
This is my second time staying here over Labor Day weekend. I returned because the housekeeping, pool staff, and valet team are all wonderful professional, kind, and welcoming. Unfortunately, the front desk experience has once again been very disappointing.

On both visits, there were booking and service issues that I brought to the front desk, and both times I was met with dismissive and unhelpful responses. As someone who has worked in the hotel industry as a Front Office Manager, I know how critical the first impression at the front desk is. If a guest has a problem, it should be an opportunity to turn the situation around whether that’s with an upgrade, a drink voucher, or even just a genuine effort to resolve the issue with care.

The front desk sets the tone for the entire stay, and if that interaction is poor, it overshadows all the positive aspects of the property. For the rates charged here, investing $10–20 in guest recovery when issues arise is a small price to pay for guest satisfaction and loyalty.

Until improvements are made with the front office staff, I would hesitate to recommend this hotel to friends despite the excellent service from the other departments.

Secondly, he offered an astronomical rate for the "cheapest" nightly fee of $2000 per night when the conference offered $389 per night for a booking rate. When I told him that we would not be going with his offering  he hung up on me. The absolute worst service I have ever received from a luxury hotel.

reviews.text: Let me first say, this trip was the Best!!! Besides my 1st time experiencing the dust storm that scared me lol! Arriving to the hotel was where it all started. I must say Ashley @ the Front Desk was absolutely awesome! She not only checked me in but she pay close attention to me rambling about everything!!! I arrive to my room and a few minutes later I received a gift from the hotel, all from Ashley listening while checking me in. People have no idea how much that means. She paid attention and was very attentive. Me being an Operations Manager at a hotel had me take notes because my hotel slacking. LOL!!!  Everyone I encountered at the desk was awesome. From Brad to Abel when I checked out. The team “Wow” me in so many ways. The Conceirge Shannon assisted me and gave me so many different place to check out. I must saying the staff at the Phoenician made me feel at home. I absolutely not only Love this place but the staff here is Top Tier! I truly appreciate each and everyone of you. It’s extremely hard to come by excellent customer services, you guys have definitely surpassed that!! I will definitely be back!!

reviews.text: The 24 hour pools was the best part in my opinion.  There are not too many hotels that keep their pools open 24 hours.  The rooms were very spacious and clean.

reviews.text:
Beautiful property, clean and beautiful rooms overlooking the cactus garden. The level of service was top notch. Tiffany, the concierge greeted us prior to arriving. Helped us get an early check-in, which was much appreciated. As we checked in at the service desk, Ben was great and helped us select a beautiful room. When it came to dinner, I reached out to Ben and he suggested a wonderful Mexican restaurant which was outstanding. Truly appreciated. Even the valet service personally delivered our bags to our room by the time we checked in and got into the room.

Overall, this was an amazing experience and I will happily come back. 😁

reviews.text: A Marriott luxury collection at the Phoenician. What a wonderful place for either a couple or families to take a vacation. Despite the heat of 106° if you go in the summer. From check in to checking out, it was definitely first class all the way. The staff, in the hotels, and the restaurants and the shops were absolutely welcoming and helpful, and whatever you were looking for. The rooms were pristine and clean, and the room service was great. It had three levels of pools, with things to do for kids they had a slide, and a activity list. For adults, they had a nice pool bar. There is also a full-fledged spa, and lots of shops to look through. The area is well kept, and beautiful. I would get this place five stars all the way around, 10 if it would allow me.!
reviews.author: Debi LaStarza

reviews.text:
What a stunning property! Beautiful views from the rooms with a good sized balcony. Service was incredible from the second we pulled up. Kevin helped us to the room with our luggage and Price at the front desk was super friendly and welcoming. Paula, the head concierge, helped us with all of our dining reservations and spa appointments. Thank you so much! My wife LOVED the spa!
We had fun playing in the various pools and splash pad with the kids. The food and drinks around the pool were phenomenal!
Elena in housekeeping did a phenomenal job with stay over services.
The restaurants on site were outstanding. Dino the bartender in lobby bar and servers Jazmine and Courtney were amazing!
Thank you for your help with the reservation Joanna! We will be back. Highly recommend a staycation or staying here when visiting from out of state!!!

reviews.text:
Very good but not 5 star.

We arrived early at 10:30 and were able to get into our rooms upon arrival. That is always a plus, the downside was it didn’t appear the room was fully prepared for the new guest as there were half empty water bottles that greeted us on the table and a funky stain on the chaise lounge (pic included). The room was large, but felt a bit dated. A surprise for us was the bidet in the bathroom, not common in American hotels.

My wife had a facial at the spa and I played the golf course on site. Both were good, just not 5 star good. Dinner was also on site at the Tavern the first night and that experience was 5 star.

During our stay we had breakfast in the room and at Mowry and Cotton and those meals and service were 5 star.

Accommodations at the pool were a bit strange to have cushioned lounge chairs at the family pool but not at the adult only pool. Hence, most couples even without children went to the family pool. In regards to the cushions on the lounge chairs, they were filthy and strained. I would never lay on one with out a towel. See pictures attached. The Phoenician needs to invest in new pool seating and side tables as many were damaged.

Service at the pool was a 3 at best our first few days, but a 5 on our last day with John providing great service poolside.

The Phoenician is a very good option for a stay in the area, just not a 5 star experience.

reviews.text: It was too busy but nice.

reviews.text: Loved my stay here! The property sits right at the foot of Camelback Mountain and is just beautiful. Loved seeing all the oleander around the hotel, and local plants all around. The rooms are enormous. I appreciated they had an "adults only" pool so there was a quiet, kid free area to relax. My only small complaint is I stayed in a casita, and if you come back to your room somewhat late at night (past 10 pm), I couldn't figure out a way to get to my casita without walking through the sprinkler system. reviews.text: The late checkout is not free. I called ahead to make sure there is late check out. Because I was bringing my dog. And my spa appointment with family was at 12PM. On the day of departure at 7:30AM, I went to the front desk to confirm the late check out. The front desk manager told me the hotel was sold out. So my late check out was denied. I said I have a dog and my spa is at 12PM. She said she can give me 2 hours for $150. I asked why I was not informed prior to my arrival on the phone and during check in. The front desk manager said the late check out fee is not advertised. I commented there is inconsistent of hotel policy among employees. Maybe they need to address it. The front desk manager said "I'm not going to argue with you. I can only give you the late check out this one time. And I'm going to write on your profile that no future late check out." I'm not sure she wrote on my Marriot profile or Phoenician hotel profile. I'm very disappointed with Phoenician hotel in Arizona. I stayed there when it was a Starwood hotel several times. I think the good reviews were from back then. I'd highly recommend to check Trip adviser recent reviews. The bad reviews were all true.

For the price I'd stay at a Four Seasons tbh

The below is a combination of highs and lows. I was trying to email this but the app and staff never responded with a way to email the feedback

-HIGHLIGHT of the stay was Sydney at the Tavern. I called and placed a pick up order which i know isn’t common. She took full ownership of the request and took care of everything. The order was accurate and even took note of my special requests. She made it seamless, pleasant, and with a sense of urgency and ownership
-Micah in room service was great, very solid and professional.
-banquet/catering food, esp proteins were stellar, not dry either

OPPORTUNITIES:
-main ballroom bathrooms - too many soap dispensers were out. however they were mostly clean but I would have more frequent check ups during large groups
-locked out of my room twice. First time security had to reprogram my lock with a special device. Second time security had to go get me a new set of keys after testing mine. Casitas
-i went to the registration desk to get new keys after leaving mine in the room. Security stated the keys were not programmed correctly and kept me locked out the second time. -However the huge issue was the registration desk. 1 manager and 1 associate were at the desk. Manager was checking in one lady which took the entire 15-16 minutes. Didn’t seem to be any issues, he was just explaining every detail of the hotel which is a tricky thing to balance. The associate was with a guest for even longer. Another manager, bearded, shows up half way through my wait and has zero sense of urgency and a bit too relaxed and kept walking around. 3 others were behind me for nearly the entire 15 minutes which i was shocked to see no call for assistance or an MOD step in sooner. Another person in a blazer walks behind the desks twice but not sure of their role. Also the manager that did show would later state that the computers were not functioning correctly on the two he tried which just exasperates the situation and the crazy long delay. How you balance information with check in speeds is tricky but what seems to be lacking is being on toes and no sense of urgency or sympathy for the long waits.
-Jenn in room service speaks way too fast and seemed like a veteran here. That speed of hers combined with zero emotion, vs a sense of warmth, makes the entire room service ordering process feel extremely rushed and uncomfortable. reviews.text:
A Beautiful Stay with Room for Improvement

The Phoenician Resort is undeniably stunning, from the breathtaking mountain views near our hotel room to the beautifully landscaped grounds, multiple pool options, and towering palm trees that truly make the resort feel like a desert oasis. However, while the scenery impressed us, several aspects of our stay fell short, especially when compared to other top resorts in the Phoenix area.

Dining & Amenities:
One major concern was the limited dining hours. Most on-site restaurants closed by 5:00 PM, with The Tavern being the only option open until 8:00 PM. As out-of-town guests, this left us with little choice in the evenings aside from room service or ordering out. We expected more flexibility and variety in a luxury resort.

Shops & Pool Experience:
All shops on the property also closed early at 5:00 PM, and pool amenities, including the water slide, music, bar, and even the water fountains, were shut down around the same time. This was disappointing, as the pool is typically a hub of activity and relaxation, especially in the summer.

Children's Activities:
We were especially let down by the Funicians Kids Club, which was never open during our stay. This was a major reason we selected the Phoenician, and our children were incredibly disappointed by its unavailability.

Summer Activities:
We appreciated the advertised “Legendary Summers” theme, but there were no events scheduled during the weekdays only on the weekends. Other Phoenix-area resorts we’ve visited provide daily family-friendly activities all summer long, so the lack of weekday activities was a letdown.

Overall, while the resort is visually impressive and offers a serene setting, we felt the guest experience didn’t fully match the high rating and reputation. With a few key improvements especially around extended hours, family activities, and consistent activites the Phoenician could offer a truly legendary experience to match its branding.
reviews.author: Keristin Jones

reviews.text: Had an excellent time at the Phoenician for our recent trip to Phoenix. The resort is massive, with tons of things to do, a large pool complex, and dedicated spa building onsite. Service throughout was exceptional and our room was well appointed/decorated. There is for sure a corporate event focus for the resort, but we were unbothered by the corporate activity/crowd during our stay. Would come back!

reviews.text: Great experience from check in to check out. Arrived 6/26, and was met at the registration desk by Brad, he was very welcoming as it was our first time in Arizona, we were given a room upgrade :) unexpectedly but appreciated. We asked questions and Brad gave us the answers he also recommended places to eat and visit while on our stay. Our room was nice we had a spacious balcony and a view of the pool. reviews.text:
Date: 06/14/25

Title: “The Best of the Best”

Pros:

* Guarded checkpoint at the main entrance

* a luxurious resort entrance with Camelback Mountain in the backdrop.

* Several accommodation options on site including under ground parking. With a fully functional parking garage.

* I was very surprised how they were able to bring the classic luxury experience into 2025.

* Valet is always available to assist you at the main entrance with all of your transportation needs day or night.

* The main lobby entrance is very grand and opulent with people catering to your every need and fountains I mean the whole nine yards.

* This location offers a true resort experience almost as if you’re away in another country.

* It’s located in one of the best locations in Scottsdale across from Old Town Scottsdale and adjacent to Paradise Valley.

* They have several eating options on site. Such as The Markerplace adjacent to the main lobby which is like a cafe bistro. Across from that is an actual convenience store like shop within the hotel. They have Mowry & Cotton which has a great everyday food menu with class. They also have The Tavern which is like a pub with excellent food options but more casual. They have a restaurant at the pool named Kalio. You can get food also at Thirsty Camel which is the lobby bar that has excellent food options. The crown jewel is J&G steakhouse with excellent service and views of Camelback Mountain. And lastly they have 24/7 room service.

* onsite there are several activities and venues such as the Athletic Center, Tennis Courts, Game Room, Golf Center, Several Pools with a slide, The Phoenician Spa and even a kids center called Funicians Club.

* There are 645 total accommodations: 577 guest rooms and 68 suites. Guest rooms span 600 square feet; suites are twice that size with one or two bedrooms. I stayed in a Grand Deluxe King w/ pool view this trip which was lovely like a mini suite. In the past I have stayed in the large suites which is just as lovely with more space. The rooms have a very classic feel but are still very modern and updated.

* They have the Canyon Suites on-site which is a separate hotel within a hotel. I will review that one at a later date. Although it’s supposed to have a more personalized luxury experience.

* $100 incidental per night and a $50 resort fee per night

* Romantic/Nature Inspired Cactus Garden across from the main lobby entrance.

Cons:

* no house car anymore for everyone except VIP and people staying at the canyon suites. To be honest I’m mentioning this because it was an experience when they did have it. But of course Ubers are readily available.

* there was no trash bin in my bathroom. Just overall there should have been more small trash bins in the room I had.

* The property is very large. There are so many things available to do and see. Although they do provide you with a guide at check in. It would be nice to have property tours if they don’t already have this.

* There were so many shops/food options available on-site that I had no idea about until I literally toured the whole property.

Summary:

This is the place that you stay when you have finally made it in life. Anything you want or need is here on site or close by including the stunning views of Camelback Mountain. If you’re looking for a true resort experience this place provides that and more. I believe my title for this place says it all.

Thumbs Up Or Down: Thumbs Up

Key People:

Devin - Front Desk (a true GEM for the property with his knowledge and skillset with the charisma to match)

Javier - Front Desk (another star I encountered on site. He checked me in and was able to determine exactly the experience I was looking for and he nailed it)

Chad - Bell desk (exceptional service, remembered my name, and made me feel special and valued each time I encountered him)

Dino - Bartender (he may be the best mixologist in Phoenix)

Sydney - Hostess (The Tavern) - very knowledgeable and helpful when explaining the menu and the property.

reviews.text:
I stayed here for a work conference last week and was very impressed overall by the layout of the resort. The staff were all very friendly and easy to work with. The views are pretty incredible (mountains, pools, golf course, cactus’, etc.). They have a restaurant located in the hotel on the first floor (near the pools). They also have a lobby bar that had great service but is extremely pricey. There are several convenience/retail stores as well as a coffee shop.

The room was very spacious and had a massive patio. The bathroom was beautiful and had a shower and a separate large tub. The elevators can be a bit confusing as there are no buttons once you are inside, but you’ll figure it out after a day or two. Room service came twice a day (which was a first for me at any hotel).

The gym—absolutely beautiful and has everything you need! I almost never use gyms at hotels but am sure glad I checked it out. They also have tennis courts and a basketball court.

On the last night I noticed a bed bug in one of the beds in my room (see last video in my review)…that put a damper in my experience. I mentioned it upon checking out (not as a complaint but a warning that they should clean the room extra well). I’m hoping to get a refund for that last night but haven’t heard back from management.

Other than that, I had a wonderful experience here! Between the pools, the views, and the staff, it was a wonderful week. But…be on the lookout for bed bugs.

reviews.text: As an Arizona local, I’ve stayed at almost all the resorts in town. A staycation in the summer time somehow makes the 110 degrees much more bearable. I have been to the Phoenician many times before this, but this was my first time staying at the Canyon Suites. I wanted something more quiet and serene. I knew the main pool had a tendency to get packed with people and seems cater more towards families and kids with the water slide. So, I opted for the Canyon Suites because it is disconnected from the main building, has its own pool, close to the fitness center and a beautiful view of Camelback mountain. When I arrived, I had been upgraded (Marriott member). Woohoo! Max, who checked me what so nice and accommodating. My room was beautiful! Overlooking the pool with the mountain in the background. It had a separate living and dining room area, bathtub and a gorgeous balcony. I went down to the pool. It wasn’t crowded at all. The nice man, can’t remember his name, greeted me to set up my chair. I feel so bad for the people who work in this extreme heat, so I tipped him $10. He did not want to take it and was so gracious. Then I was greeted by Sharon, my pool server, who was fantastic! She brought over a free root beer float sample, right when I sat down. She was attentive, not overbearing. I ordered food and drinks. She was so sweet! She knew everyone’s name. Maybe the best service I’ve ever had poolside. The food was great - it’s the same menu as the spa, so it’s healthy and light. I was only there for 1 night but it was such a relaxing, lovely experience. The staff was incredible and I highly recommend the Canyon Suites - if you’re looking for a quiet getaway.

reviews.text: The Phoenician gets 10s across the board from me. I’m a former Marriott employee who wanted to celebrate my birthday early & their property, service & location is unmatched. (I came Memorial Day weekend which turned out to be very eventful.) I ate at Mowry & Cotton, Thirsty Camel & Kalio Kabbobery and the restaurants are consistent! The food is downright tasty. reviews.author: ul8ra

reviews.text:
Let me start by saying: now I understand why this resort isn’t rated higher.

We just wrapped up a week-long trip to Arizona, and unfortunately, The Phoenician—our final stop—left us disappointed. For a property that positions itself as luxury, the experience felt more like a series of hidden fees and lackluster service. From unexpected porter charges to an overall feeling of being nickel-and-dimed, it simply didn’t deliver on the value.

One of the most unsettling parts of our stay was the check-in process. Not only was it disorganized and slow, but the way we were treated compared to other guests was noticeably different. I don’t make assumptions lightly—but the energy and lack of courtesy felt borderline discriminatory. It’s 2025. That should never be part of anyone’s travel experience.

Also worth noting: if you’re a Marriott Bonvoy member—especially with elite status—don’t expect your loyalty to be honored here. The usual recognition and perks seem nonexistent at this property.

The resort itself needs serious development in both hospitality and professionalism. For the price point and the brand name, I expected more—and frankly, I expected better. Would not return.
reviews.author: tatum vacation

reviews.text: We stayed Saturday over Memorial Day weekend. The last time we were here 7 years ago the experience was amazing. This time was different. The pool experience was abysmal. They had no one at any of the towel stations and had run out of towels. They had to go scrounge them from somewhere for practically everyone at the pool. Maybe a third of the chairs had pool covers. When they finally brought towels they were threadbare with holes. Questionable whether they had even been washed. There were no side tables to put water or drinks near our chairs. The one they found had holes in it and barely held up the water pitcher. The splash pad wasn’t fully functional either. Very disappointed since we came specifically for a pool experience for our kids. The staff were very apologetic and tried to be helpful it seems like they were set up for failure by the management. As for the room, it was above average. The food was excellent but the restaurant seemed understaffed. With all the options for resorts in town I would not come back or recommend the Phoenician. Again, the staff were all great but seems like it is suffering from poor management.

reviews.text:
We were extremely disappointed with our recent stay at The Phoenician, which unfortunately fell far short of the "luxury resort" experience it promises.

The most shocking part of our visit was discovering a cockroach in our bed, under the covers, in our hotel room. To make matters worse, our room was located directly next to the garbage area—on the third floor—which we believe may explain how the cockroach got in.

The room itself was also outdated and did not reflect the luxurious feel portrayed on the resort’s website, nor the outrages price for what you get. We chose The Phoenician to try something new, even though we've previously had excellent experiences at the Andaz. Sadly, this was a mistake.

When I showed the photo of the cockroach to the receptionist, they visibly jolted in shock—but to their credit, they handled the situation very professionally. They kindly comped our room, which we appreciated, and we immediately checked out and moved to the Andaz - an incredibly inconvenient process that ended up wasting hours of our vacation. Instead of relaxing, we had to pack up, leave, and coordinate a new stay at another resort.. Not only was The Andaz resort more affordable(which I still cant comprehend), our experience at the Andaz was once again outstanding and felt like we were genuienly taken care of—just as we remembered.

What struck us as particularly odd was that, despite the seriousness of the issue, no one from the management team came out to apologize. The receptionist went to speak with them and explained the situation, yet there was no follow-up or acknowledgment from management. That lack of accountability was disappointing.

In summary, The Phoenician felt more like a Motel 6 than a high-end resort. While the front desk staff did their job well, the overall experience was unacceptable. We won’t be returning and strongly recommend the Andaz resort instead—it’s truly a dream resort and everything we were looking for.
reviews.author: Raeven Peterson

reviews.text: We stayed here for 5 nights. Beautiful! Stunning resort full of some of the best customer service I've seen! We got an amazing view of camelback mountain and was super nice. Only 3 complaints, 1. The rooms is your average hotel room nothing really else about it, we had a 2 queen. 2. Not a whole lot for older kids to do besides to hangout at the pool. 3. It's very expensive, in my opinion it's not the best value for your money and everything is super pricey, but if you have the money I would definitely stay here. Rooms were very clean and staff was super friendly. Definitely the best hotel I've stayed at but I would recommend to try to go around and enjoy scottsdale/pheonix. We went on the cactus walk and it was a nice chill walk and very relaxing. Pools were very nice and even heated to a bathtub temperature of water. When i was there one of the hot tubs was cold and so I went to they adult one which was very hot. At night the pools change color from blue, green, red. One of the best experiences I've had!
