reviews.text:
Disappointed by Outdated Rooms and Lack of Upkeep – Far from a 5-Star Experience

As a frequent luxury traveler and hospitality reviewer, I had high expectations for The Phoenician given its longstanding reputation as one of Arizona’s premier resorts. While the natural setting of the property is undeniably beautiful, the overall experience unfortunately fell short of what one would expect from a resort commanding $900–$1,000 per night.

To begin with, I want to commend the staff, who were gracious and clearly made efforts to ensure our stay was as pleasant as possible. Their professionalism and willingness to assist did not go unnoticed. However, service alone cannot compensate for the physical condition of the accommodations, which were frankly quite disappointing.

The guest rooms are in serious need of renovation. The design and furnishings felt dated, but more concerning were the cleanliness and maintenance issues. Black mold was visible in the showers, vents were caked with dust, and we encountered multiple bugs in the room—issues that are unacceptable at any level of hospitality, let alone a luxury property. HVAC systems appeared neglected, contributing to poor air quality and discomfort.

At its current state, the rooms reflect the experience of a mid-tier hotel priced at $200 per night—not a luxury resort nearing four figures. Unless there is a significant and comprehensive overhaul of the rooms and facilities, I cannot in good faith recommend The Phoenician as a 5-star destination. I will not be returning until the resort undergoes a transformation that aligns its offerings with its pricing and reputation.

reviews.author: Samantha Smith

reviews.text:
Attention any families with young kids wanting to come here:
The rooms are not luxury at all and disgusting. The carpet is from 30 years ago and the rooms haven’t been updated probably since. The outdoor patio furniture is old and stained and the floor is GROSS. The coffee machine in here is an old Kerig (most luxury marriot properties have Nespresso). Oh and there’s no complimentary coffee anywhere. You have to go all the way down to the breakfast restaurant to even find it on property. One morning my husband had to buy from their marketplace because the basement coffee wasn’t available and he spent $19 for two regular coffees. Two!

There is nothing to accommodate little kids. The four seasons gave us little stuffed animals and mini robes. Here, nothing. The kids club have a couple random activities for older kids at random times (mainly during nap time).

The customer service is abysmal. I asked a server for a glass so I can have some juice at the buffet I was paying for and he said I should go back to my table and get it myself…. The servers at the pool were rude too and don’t act like an even 3 star resort.

The food on property is also horrendous. All claiming to be high end and luxury but it is anything but. Room service, terrible. The pool food is decent but it takes an hour to receive it. There’s no fast casual place to pick up food for little kids. We had to drive off property most days.

The pool area was also atrocious. There barely were any attendants helping with towels, you have to hunt them down. No one cleans up, there’s trash everywhere and all of the chairs are gross and stained. There was also trash all over the resort.

They also don’t comp parking if you are staying at the resort, which just feels like another way they can squeeze every last dollar from you.

For the amount of money we are spending here it’s a huge disappointment. Next time I’ll stay at a four seasons or the ritz for these prices.

Oh and a sandwich at their “marketplace” was $20 for one! Highway robbery!

Also worth noting we are lifetime gold members and they didn’t do anything for us either.
reviews.author: Sara Norman

reviews.text:
It’s ok. Overpriced for sure. Rooms are nice. Staff is very hit and miss. Some are really good and some have no business working here. I would not call it a particularly kids friendly place and it does advertise that. There are some kids stuff but any child over 5 will be bored fast.

C+

Also, when did having a bit of money make people stupid? Two adult salads and two kids pastas for room service. $175
Morning regular brewed coffee. $6.

I’m sorry. Stuff like this is insulting to the guests. I’m fine paying fine dining when it’s appropriate. But just “double the cost” of everything in a resort with an average pool, an even more average golf course. Come on.

People might be fine paying that but I’m not. I’ll never come to this resort again just because they are clearly ripping people off on their food costs.
reviews.author: seanqwerty2000

reviews.text:
We came The Phoenician for the 3rd time for Spring Break. Full disclosure: it was a last minute trip and we selected the most affordable room with two queen beds but it was still $850+ per night. We had had great experiences in our past two trips so it seemed like a safe bet. Initially I noticed the hall on the walk to our room smelled faintly of urine - like the floor of an old pub - but the room seemed fine so I let it go. On day two of our trip we noticed an intense plumbing/sewage smell outside our room and in parts of our room. We left and came back and the smell was still there. I called the front desk and they assured me they’d send an engineer immediately. Someone walking down the hall literally said “it smells like poop.” Forty five minutes later no one showed and I waited on hold for the front desk for 10 minutes before walking down to discuss in person. I explained the situation and they agreed to move us to a casita that “I would love.” As we were packing up the room the engineer showed up with a cleaning spray. Not a chance that was going to be sufficient. We got to the casita and the room was nice but had double beds instead of queens which doesn’t work for a family of four. We were moved again to a room with two queens. This room had a concrete wall outside the tiny patio. Literally a wall. After going back to the front desk AGAIN I was advised they were at very high capacity and options were slim. I get that they can’t change that. We ended up in a 4th room that is dark and down at the farthest end of the hotel. The recording while I was on hold with the front desk repeated that this Luxury Collection is for the discerning traveler. We are long time Marriott members with Titanium Elite status. I understand that the staff could not magic me a better room but I got the continued feeling that staff was doing whatever was going to move me along the fastest. There was a lack of care and more a ticking of the box of ‘problem technically handled.’ That’s not a luxury approach. This is three star treatment at five star prices. I was not treated as a discerning traveler. This ruined my day. Ruined my dinner plans. Ruined my trip. Will not return. Would not recommend.

Other notable mentions: Pool staff was very good and friendly but stretched too thin. Shout out to Gennaro. Bryan in bell service was wonderful. Gloria at Mowry + Cotton was amazing.

reviews.text: We have stayed multiple times at the Phoenician and have never had a bad experience. Our most recent stay- March 2025- was no different. reviews.text: I absolutely suggest you stay at one of Scottsdale’s many other resorts. This place is absolutely awful. I’m still on property, generally they run a shotty three star Marriot service level. rooms were not ready on time, they promised they would call or text when they were, they never texted. they couldn’t get me a reservation to the restaurant here even though I’m a guest, however, when we saw the restaurant half the tables were open at the time we wanted. I tried to call the front desk four different times from my room, nobody ever picks up. The original reservation was supposed to be at 4 PM check out which I get through Amex, they forgot to put that on there. bellman were supposed to take our luggage for four hours and left it out the entire time with absolutely nobody guarding it, and it was only just luck that nobody stole the contents. Hopefully you get the idea. This is not someplace you want to stay, especially if you’re spending more than $1000 a night. The real kicker, the front desk wouldn’t even give me the email address of the GM. They said he was too important and it had to go through his assistant. I’ve stayed at fine hotels around the world, that’s a first. But it’s emblematic of why this place runs so poorly. It’s a shame. It’s a beautiful property, but terribly managed.

reviews.text:
The Phoenician in Arizona was a massive disappointment. Despite my partner’s Marriott Gold Elite status, a promised room upgrade was revoked, and the front desk’s dismissive response added insult to injury. Room service failed us twice, never delivering a simple knife and bowl for my service animal, despite the resort claiming to be pet-friendly.

Dinner options were limited to the J&G Steakhouse, where the manager, Mike, behaved aggressively and unprofessionally. He physically grabbed my shoulder, verbally berated us, and questioned my service animal in a condescending manner. Although he eventually backed down, his hostility ruined our evening. Staff at the bar apologized, but the damage was done. The night manager’s offer of two glasses of wine was insulting, and no meaningful resolution was provided.

Mike’s behavior was unacceptable, and it’s shocking that this has reportedly happened before. For a resort that claims 5-star status, the experience was appalling. Avoid at all costs.

reviews.text: Location is lovely, service good, rooms good. Food is ok. Restaurant is small for such a massive resort and food quality / fine just reasonably good for the PRICE they ask. Which is absolutely premium. Last breakfast colleagues took things like toast with avocado and it was $38. Hamburger topped the $50 price I was told. Then there are all sorts of charges / extras on your bill like porterage (not used) and something for housekeeping which I can only imagine was cost for refilling of the minibar as I didn’t use housekeeping during my stay. where the products are as always very highly priced anyway.  The lack of restaurant space meant most food was served outside (with those “mushroom” gas fired heaters around)  and therefore in the shape of buffets and in the cold, make sure you dress for that!  All in all a good experience we had fun. Just be aware as a family what you step into, it is truly premium
reviews.author: Marc

reviews.text:
We recently hosted a conference for 70 guests at The Phoenician, and I can say with complete confidence that it was an unforgettable experience. From the moment we arrived, we were blown away by the beauty of the property—The Phoenician is absolutely stunning, with its lush landscapes, elegant design, and luxurious atmosphere. It’s a truly special place.

What truly made our event exceptional, however, was the incredible staff. From the very first planning meeting to the final moments of our conference, the team went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect. Their attention to detail, professionalism, and warm hospitality made every step of the process seamless and enjoyable. It’s clear that the team at The Phoenician is dedicated to providing an outstanding experience, and they certainly delivered.

Not only was the venue beautiful, but the service was flawless. The event spaces were well-equipped and thoughtfully arranged, and the catering and amenities were outstanding. Our guests had nothing but praise for every aspect of the event.

We’re so grateful to The Phoenician for making our conference an absolute success. It’s rare to work with a team that combines exceptional service with such a breathtaking location. We look forward to returning and highly recommend The Phoenician to anyone seeking a perfect venue for their event!

reviews.text:
Day before arriving, (12/30) I called to confirm my stay as I had booked with AmEx. Was told by Brad the reservation was cancelled. Spent over an hour on the phone with AmEx to learn Marriott didn’t have permission to cancel AND had not notified myself or AmEx. Brad was seemingly helpful, but suggested to me to “re-book” which would have been at a higher rate. I refused and AmEx resolved that issue.
Arrived the next day (12/31) at 130 and checked in. At 4 pm, the advertised checkin time, my room wasn’t ready. At 4:35 I went to the front desk and was told the room wasn’t ready, BUT if I wanted to move to a lower level floor they could check me in. One person, who I won’t mention by name, for fear of him being punished for his honesty, told me point blank it was a lesser room than I had booked and paid for and not to move. I then asked to speak with Brad, who acted the day before as if he was in a position of authority. Brad told me the room wasn’t a downgrade and if I “really wanted to check-in then I should just take the room that was available.” No, thank you and you are dishonest. When I asked for my 5 pm dinner reservation to be moved, I was questioned why that would be necessary. Let’s see, it’s 440, I’ve been traveling, need to change and YOU still don’t have me in a room. Reluctantly, Brad/Bryce called and moved the reservation to later.
From there we had the worst service. Waited for service EVERY single time at Mowry & Cotton. Ordered hot tea with drinks, it came out 20+ minutes later. Ordered more cream cheese for a bagel, it never was brought. Plates stacked everywhere outside from the breakfast buffet, including on our table inside, and no server to clear or clean them up for 30+ minutes. Birds flying everywhere and eating off plates because it was a mess anytime we dined outside. Felt like we were dining in a scene from the Birds movie! The bird man did what he could to keep the birds away, but nothing helps when dirty dishes are left sitting for lengthy periods!
On 1/3 the server outside at Thirsty Camel was painfully slow. Ended up going inside to get more drinks where she proceeded to make a comment about us not waiting. We waited and waited AND we were the only people outside. Glasses and plates stacked outside and not cleaned up for over an hour while we sat there. We ended up moving all the glasses to the other side of the fire pit to get them out of our way.
Amanda, at the pool, was great. She was kind, prompt. She deserves a raise.
I stayed at Phoenician Suites years ago and the service was impeccable. I convinced my boyfriend and his kids to join us this trip and was embarrassed I recommended this hotel.
I can unequivocally say the service was not 5 star, in most cases it was barely a 2. There is ZERO reason to return and pay the prices being charged and receive terrible service. Brad is in serious need of being trained!
Calling yourself a 5 star resort is like Carnival claiming to be a 5 star cruise ship. I don’t cruise, but if I was, it wouldn’t be on Carnival. I do enjoy 5 star resorts, but NOT this one anymore. Sadly.
reviews.author: Carrie OBrien

reviews.text:
Went to the pool on the resort day pass. First, it looked like I was getting the final day bed but when I arrived the pool was empty. Made the best of the day with no one around and ordered food/drink.
When the bill came we received an additional resort fee of $40. When we questioned the Phoenician they said we had to go through resort pass and then vice-versa. So no one took ownership of the charge and I had already paid the resort fee, so why was I charged another resort fee?!
Point is, I believe we could have just arrived without paying resort pass and then ordered poolside.

reviews.text:
The Phoenician, a Luxury Collection Resort in Scottsdale, offers an enjoyable and upscale experience overall. The facilities are impressive, with a beautifully maintained spa and a gym that is top-notch. The on-site restaurants are well-kept, providing a pleasant dining atmosphere.

We stayed in the casitas, which are townhouse-style accommodations located around the main hotel building. The convenience of parking right outside the unit was a great perk. However, the room itself felt a bit small, and the building seemed dated, which detracted slightly from the otherwise luxurious experience.

The breakfast for Marriott elite members is only a yogurt parfait and a coffee. You can get other items on their menu for extra fee. So it’s very easy to pay $50 to $80 to get what you want. We just came from a JW Marriott that had an amazing breakfast for its members. I highly recommend they improve that. The main reason we picked this hotel was it’s a part of Marriott.

While the resort is clearly making efforts to maintain its charm, some areas could benefit from further updates to match the high standards associated with its reputation. Nevertheless, The Phoenician remains a good choice for a relaxing getaway in Scottsdale, especially if you value amenities and serene surroundings.

reviews.text:
At the Phoenician Resort, member of the Marriott Luxury Collection, the authentic Mother-of-Pearl tiles were imported from Italy for $1 million to create the illustrious resort centerpiece known as the “Mother of Pearl” serenity pool. The tiles were hand-laid at the bottom of the pool to create a glistening, iridescent sanctuary – much like the inside of a sea shell.

Over the last 32 years, I have visited this pool seven times. It was always for adults only, but changed somewhere between our visits in 2016 and 2021. We met people from all over the world that reserved their cabanas a year in advance for the next year. It was quiet, beautiful, serene and spiritual.

Under any circumstance, when asked to imagine my happy place, I always imagine going underwater in the beautiful Mother of Pearl pool. Other guests have confirmed the serenity in the pool is like a sense of healing or spirituality.

In my home, you will find multiple pictures of the Mother of Pearl pool and the cabana looking towards Camelback Mountain, and also from the inside of the cabana across the Mother of Pearl pool. Last time I was here, I even took a video just walking through the pool with the sun shimmering on the Mother of Pearl tiles. I’ve played this video many times in anxious situations.

I am sad to say it has greatly changed. It is filled with Styrofoam noodles and children screaming at the top of their lungs and little babies crying. It has become the kiddie pool! Parents aren’t paying attention to the children. People not paying for the reserved cabana area are using my reserved towels. There is no pool etiquette; no etiquette in general. The younger attendants have no control.

Times have certainly changed, and I believe that The Phoenician is not the worthy of the mark as Luxury Collection it once was, but it is more serving of the mass market. So be careful if you are expecting something more exclusive. It is not what it was. Our first two nights we did not receive turn down service nor was our room cleaned before 6:00 PM. The managers on duty tried to correct the situation however we shouldn’t have to ask to have the room cleaned if we are paying an extraordinary amount a night and expect a level of service as Platinum members from the Marriott Luxury Collection. Maybe we’re paying the full price rack rate and others got a discount on Priceline? I never thought to look. So, my question is do we need to go to the level of Ritz Carlton to get what we expect? We are.

reviews.text:
I recently stayed at The Phoenician in Scottsdale with my wife and kids, and after reading all the glowing reviews, I just don’t understand the hype. It was fine, but I wouldn’t call it luxury by any means, nor exceptional, especially considering the price or the points required for a stay here. As a Gold Elite member with years of travel experience, I’ve come to recognize top-notch service and value, but this resort falls short in nearly every category.

First impressions matter, and our check-in experience wasn’t great. We didn’t feel welcomed or even like we were at a luxury resort. The staff member who checked us in barely explained anything about the property—just handed me a map and a booklet and sent us on our way.
The main pool area was closed for maintenance, and the kids' splash park wasn’t working when we tried to use it—not once, but twice. The only other pool available for kids was cold! Honestly, no one else was in it because it felt unheated, and after talking to a few guests, they agreed it was too cold. We also didn’t see any pool attendants around to ask about life jackets or pool toys, or anything that might make the experience better if the pool was heated.

The kids' club or play area was also closed on Monday, so there was literally nothing for our kids to do for the first couple of days of our stay. Fortunately, we had a larger unit with a hot tub and a golf cart to get around, which helped salvage the experience—without that, there wouldn’t have been much to do.

Speaking of the hot tub, not good. After using it on Sunday, the next day all of us had rashes or skin breakouts. We suspect it was from the excessive chlorine, as there was an unusually thick layer of foam and bubbles in the tub. Our 5-year-old, 1.5-year-old, and both adults all had reactions.

Room 7704 itself was disappointing, especially for the price and points required. It’s showing its age—there were missing pieces of flooring near the dining table (my wife actually hurt her toe), cracks and dents in the walls, and the doors don’t close properly. The whole place just felt a bit run-down. I certainly wouldn’t pay thousands to stay here.

The wifi also didn’t work for our entire stay which wasn’t ideal at all. I had a couple of meetings Monday and no wifi. Costing me money to use data. We called down to have someone come up and check it out Sunday but nobody came for almost 2 hours. Called back to inform them nobody came by, kids had to go to sleep. They were going to update the ticket and have someone come by Monday. Nobody came, no follow up, nothing. Just terrible service.

We also ordered food from the Tavern one night, and it was mediocre at best—not worth the price at all. Save your money and eat elsewhere.

As a Gold Elite member, I expected better treatment, especially with pools being closed and limited activities for kids on certain days of the week. We were hoping for an upgrade to a unit with a pool, which is supposed to happen as a gold elite member (enhanced room upgrade benefit) but despite some of the other residences being vacant both nights, they didn’t offer us anything. They were more focused on charging extra for upgrades than making sure we had a better experience, even though we were loyal members with kids and limited options at the resort.

Honestly, I regret spending 240,000 points to stay here. This resort was a major disappointment overall, and I’ll definitely be looking elsewhere next time. It was a huge waste of both time and points.

I encourage others looking to spend their hard earned dollars or points to look elsewhere.

For those of you who love this place, glad you enjoyed it and had a better experience. I know it’s hard to please everyone and it’ll rarely happen but we felt overall, it simply underwhelming and not worth it.

My husband and I were celebrating our 30th anniversary at The Phoenician. We arrived and were greeted warmly by the welcoming staff. Property was absolutely beautiful and in keeping with the Five Star rating! We checked into our room
and while we were settling in we could hear babies crying loudly from adjacent walls in our suite? We waited patiently as we are parents and understand that dealing with toddlers can be challenging. However, it went on all night. Finally stopping from 4AM-7AM when we were able to rest. The next day we awoke and hubby went to golf. I went to the pool which was beautiful. We proceeded to have a lovely afternoon adventuring to the local shops and heading to the gym. That evening we went to the fabulous steak restaurant and had a fabulous meal at J&G. Only return back to the room to screaming of adjacent toddler. I called the front desk and spoke with Ana who promised to have the manager reach out to me the next day to have us moved to another room. The next day no one reached out to us so I left another message. Still no one followed up. We spent four nights and five days listening to babies scream all night long. What was to be a fabulous anniversary celebration turned into a romper room level of unexpected disappointment. We loved our meals. Loved the amenities. But relaxing in our room never happened and our many opportunities to reach out to the manager(s) on duty never followed through. This was my first visit to Arizona and although I over the scenery, I cannot say that it was even remotely relaxing. I could’ve gone to my local Omni in Dallas and had a better getaway.

reviews.text:
My husband and I just enjoyed 4 nights at the resort. Service was amazing. Javier at guest registration was very kind and accommodating. His service set the tone.

We had lunch at Maury & Cotton as soon as we arrived. The food was great and the staff was amazing. We arrived after their lunch hour which technically should only be a very limited bar menu but the manager brought us the regular menu proactively, we didn’t even ask. We were both so hungry that we would have made anything work. It was a great gesture and indication that customer service is their number one priority.

We rented cabana’s at the adult only pool which was awesome. They included the cabana with seating within, 4 lounge chairs by the pool, as well as a patio table with seating for 4. The rental could comfortably accommodate 6-8 people as long as everyone doesn’t need to be on a lounge at the same time. there were lots of other perks like snacks, several treats throughout the day, sunscreen, etc. Christine and Raymond were our attendants and both were superb, really excellent service and nice people.

We spent a day at the spa which we were both very impressed with. I had my massage with Tomas. For someone who frequently gets massages, this was one of the best by far. He was very professional and had a strong yet not unpleasant technique to tackle the knots in my back. After our services we spent the day at the private spa rooftop pool. Lee was our attendant poolside and again her service was amazing.

Our only meh feedback was the room. It was clean and everything you would expect but there was nothing exceptional about it. We were both underwhelmed but will say that the property overall made up for it.

Overall we highly recommend The Phoenician and look forward to our next stay!

I recently had the pleasure of staying at The Phoenician, a Luxury Collection Resort, Scottsdale for a 3-night event, and it was truly an unforgettable experience. From the moment I arrived, I was treated to exceptional service, stunning views, and unparalleled luxury.

The resort's grounds are breathtakingly beautiful, with lush gardens, sparkling pools, and majestic mountain vistas. My room was elegantly appointed, with a private balcony that offered stunning views of the surrounding landscape.

But what truly sets The Phoenician apart is its commitment to excellence. The staff were friendly, attentive, and went above and beyond to ensure my stay was nothing short of perfect. From the front desk to the event staff, everyone was warm, welcoming, and dedicated to providing exceptional service.

The event itself was flawlessly executed, with delicious cuisine, impeccable decor, and seamless logistics. I was thoroughly impressed by the attention to detail and the professionalism of the entire team.

Overall, I would highly recommend The Phoenician to anyone seeking a luxurious and unforgettable experience. Whether you're attending an event or simply looking for a relaxing getaway, this resort truly has it all.

Highlights:

- Stunning views and beautifully landscaped grounds
- Luxurious rooms and amenities
- Exceptional service and staff
- Flawless event execution

Don't hesitate - book your stay today and experience the ultimate in luxury and service!"

reviews.text:
My stay at The Phoenician was truly exceptional. From the moment I arrived, I was welcomed with outstanding service and attention to detail. The resort’s stunning location, nestled at the base of Camelback Mountain, provided breathtaking views and a tranquil atmosphere that made my stay unforgettable.

The accommodations were pure luxury—elegantly designed with spacious rooms, plush bedding, and a well-appointed bathroom. The attention to detail, from the nightly turndown service to the luxurious amenities, exceeded my expectations.

The resort’s amenities are top-notch. I especially enjoyed the pool area, which offered an oasis-like experience with its multiple pools, cabanas, and excellent poolside service. The golf course is beautifully maintained, and for spa enthusiasts, The Phoenician Spa is a must-visit, offering a range of treatments in a peaceful, rejuvenating setting.

Dining at The Phoenician was a highlight. The fine dining options, including Mowry & Cotton and J&G Steakhouse, served exquisite dishes with impeccable service. Every meal was a delight, with a wide variety of options for every palate.

If I had to mention one small downside, it would be that the property is quite expansive, so walking between amenities can take some time. However, the beautiful surroundings and helpful staff more than made up for this.

Overall, The Phoenician exceeded all expectations and provided a perfect blend of luxury, comfort, and top-tier service. I highly recommend this resort for anyone seeking a high-end, relaxing getaway.

Pool and waiting staff were the same quality. Our room was beautiful and spotless. Don't hesitate to book a reservation!

reviews.text:
I want to start off with the pros of my experience staying with them for labor day week;
Pros- Large rooms, beautiful clean amenities, free parking, pools allowed night swims, 18+ areas. Housekeeping was the most professional. Pool side service amazing.

**Cons:** DO NOT CHARGE TO THE ROOM. On the first day of our stay, we reserved a poolside cabana and had an excellent experience. However, when it was time to pay, the server casually mentioned, "on the room," and we agreed. Unfortunately, this led to a pending charge of $2,600 on our account on top of the cabana charge and incidentals. The resort's billing system pulls pending money based on what you've charged to the room, so they imagine what you "plan" to spend which is both confusing and problematic. We’ve stayed at numerous resorts and have never encountered such a practice. When we raised this issue with the staff, we were simply told we shouldn’t have put it on the room, as if we had been informed otherwise. It’s unacceptable for a system to lock up funds without prior notice, and we couldn’t access the money until we checked out three days later. Our bank has informed us that the funds may remain inaccessible for 7-14 more days.

Additionally, the concierge service was disappointing. The two middle-aged women working in that department were unkind. At one point, we were turned away after being directed to them by the front desk. One concierge then proceeded to sit on the floor in the center of the lobby, talking loudly to a child in an unprofessional manner until her co-worker helped her up off the floor. This behavior was unprofessional and unexpected at such a "highly established" location. Everyone was uneasy who witnessed it. The staff’s demeanor needs significant improvement and clearly needs some more proper training.

LOVED our stay here! It really did feel like a 5-star hotel—from service to amenities.

Pros:
- Resort is huge, with lots of activities and several dining options, enough for you to spend your stay here and don’t really need to leave the resort
- Decor was nice and clean, and has a fancy vibe
- Service was EXCELLENT—majority of the staff were so friendly and helpful
- Our Spacious 2 Queens Bedroom was nice with comfy beds, huge bathroom and a balcony overlooking the pool. Also received some complimentary welcome snacks after we checked in. Had a fully stocked fridge (for purchase), and room safe

Cons:
- Not enough security measures—I didn’t see security throughout most of the complex—also, just about anyone can walk around the resort, there’s no restricted card access to get to the rooms hallway area either
- There are 3 pools, but the Adults-Only pool had children and staff did nothing to request they go to the kid friendly pool—this was annoying when you expect a peaceful pool time and kids are shouting and splashing water all around
- Pool bar closes early, even around 6pm Saturday the bar was closed—resort should offer drink service because many of us would have ordered cocktails

Tonight, I ordered a pizza and the staff was kind enough to let me know that, on top of the 22% mandatory gratuity, and after the extra tip I am encouraged to add, there was a $5 “delivery fee.”  So, the total “fee” to drop off a pizza box is $10.40 for a $20 pizza = a 50%+ tip. reviews.text:
A great place to stay - especially for Bonvoy members to either rack up or use points. The resort is beautiful and impeccably maintained outside. Considerations...

Rooms: Zero complaints. I would opt for an outside building with private patio.

Gym: Excellent and well maintained equipment. Lots of treadmills and cardio machines. Free weights - dumbbells and kettlebells. Cable and smith machine. Rowing machine too! Spacious with bottled water and lots of towels. You don't have to compromise your workout on the road.

Bar: Huge bar area in main building. Great atmosphere and friendly bartenders.

Pools: Multiple. Including an adult only pool if you're not there to deal with kids. Pool area has plenty of umbrellas, lounge chairs, cabanas.

Food: Dinner at The Tavern onsite restaurant was excellent. Recommend the Pull Apart Pretzel, Stone Fruit & Arugula salad.

Overall: Great place for business stay and also a couples getaway. Can't speak to the golf course. The staff was top notch from arrival through checkout.
reviews.author: Chris H

reviews.text: This was our third year in a row visiting this destination resort and it continues to exceed expectations. Location: Considering the fact The Phoenician Resort is located in the booming metropolis of Phoenix/Scottsdale, its proximity to Camelback mountain is one redeeming factor that makes the venue even more spectacular. Service: 10 stars. Service has always been excellent, but this year, Bryce (our check-in agent at the front desk) set the bar even higher. First, he remembered our request made 3 days earlier by phone when we asked if our Casita included a Nespresso machine. (He explained the adjacent Canyon Suites have Nespresso machines, but the Casitas do not). No worries as we could bring our travel-Nespresso machine for this 4-day trip. Yet he surprised us with a welcome card, anniversary greeting and stated, "Hey since we couldn't upgrade you to the Canyon Suites, we decided to bring a little of the Canyon suites to your Casita and included the Nespresso song on our welcome card."  Now that's a concierge-level of service if I have ever seen one. The Casita's in their own right are fabulous, spacious and first class. 3 different swimming pools, a great waterslide and 4-5 restaurants on-site mean you don't need to go anywhere off property. The fitness facility is nothing short of fabulous. The Phoenician is highly recommended and a destination you won't soon forget.

reviews.text: Met my niece for cocktails as she was in town for work, great atmosphere and drinks, delicious !
reviews.author: Robin Duncan

reviews.text:
The resort is beautiful and has everything you'd want on vacation: spa, pools (adult-only as well as kid/family ones), a cactus trail, multiple restaurants etc.

We really enjoyed our vacation here.

My only complaint is that the staff is not attentive. They are very nice (except Anna at the front desk who was unhelpful when our room key was mistakenly deactivated), just not on it. In every restaurant we went to, service was slow even though they weren't really busy. At one place, we sat at a dirty table and waited 15 minutes for them to clean it. Even then, they only removed the dirty dishes and didn't bother to wipe the table down until I requested it.

Like I said the property is nice, but the inattentiveness of the staff is far below what's expected at a 5 star resort.
reviews.author: Angie Jones

reviews.text: This resort was just what the doctor ordered.  Cabana suite with fireplace did not disappoint.  Everything was top notch - the food at JG steakhouse and Mowey & Cotton was outstanding!  Took bikes for a ride to camelback thru paradise valley - beautiful!
reviews.author: fjmcpa

reviews.text: Beautiful resort! I was just visiting friends from out of town that were staying there. Fabulous destination 😎
reviews.author: Rick Klotz

reviews.text: Had an incredible experience at The Phoenician! Attentive staff who went above and beyond to make my birthday special by decorating my room with roses, balloons and champagne while I was away. Will definitely be coming back here!
reviews.author: Carly Wermers

reviews.text: I enjoyed a relaxing 3 night stay here in June 2024. The facility was exceptional in every respect. The room was spacious and attractively appointed. The bed was very comfortable and the linens were luxurious. The room service was on point, with a nice selection of original meals that were prepared with care and had a homemade feel. I had 2 meals at Mowry and Cotton as well…same kind of thing. The public spaces in the hotel were quiet and comfortable, with a sanctuary kind of feel. I am looking forward to returning.
reviews.author: Chris Moran

reviews.text:
Great facility. Conveniently located.

We dine at some of the restaurants often. And we love the live entertainment. The facility is always clean, the staff are friendly, and the atmosphere is very inviting.

Garage and valet parking available
reviews.author: O'Zandra

reviews.text: The view, the staff, the room, everything about it was great!
reviews.author: Mo Diallo

reviews.text: Spent our 4 year anniversary here. When we arrived, we were greeted by the reception and checked in quickly. The directions to our hotels room, and a few other places were provided. Walking up to the room we noticed a soda/beer stain along the wall to the right of the door directly near where you scan your card to get in. Once inside the room we were impressed by its openness, and size of the patio. 4th floor viewing the pool was quite nice. walking back into the room we noticed stains along the bedroom walls, handprints, and drip stains. Though they weren't very visible without the light beaming in. We thought about requesting a different room but didnt want to bother. The pools were nice but not as large as we'd hoped. Not as lively either. The servers poolside did a great job at ensuring we had drinks. Our dinner at JG steakhouse was spectacular, seated next to the window at sunset was a real treat. The lobby bar was very alive around 10pm. All in all we did enjoy our stay, but for the amount paid, we will likely be staying at one of the competing resorts nearby next time.
reviews.author: John Chavez

reviews.text:
I recently had another disappointing experience with the Phoenician Hotel Resort. On my second attempt to stay at the hotel, I was once again let down and had to cancel my reservations while standing at their counter due to the hotel's inability to provide me with the rooms I had reserved. -Despite a low 45% occupancy rate in mid-June, I was told that my "connected" rooms were unavailable, which seemed like a poor excuse from the management.

Frustrated with the their poor customer service, I Celtic best to move to the neighboring Sanctuary Resort, where I was pleasantly surprised by the excellent service and a much nicer room that truly reflected a five-star standard. It's apparent that the Phoenician Hotel Resort lacks proper management and falls short in delivering on their promises to guests.

While I appreciated the Sanctuary Resort's ability to accommodate me in a time of need, I would caution others about the Phoenician Hotel Resort's lack of accountability and extremely lazy approach to customer satisfaction.
reviews.author: Rodney Nielsen

reviews.text:
Good afternoon Catering friend ( I didn´t find any name for catering managers on your website :(

It is a pleasure to meet you and make the following request:
We would like to host a presentation dinner for the destination of Chihuahua on October 8th for 30 people.
Please I need an estimate including filet mignon for the mayority of guests or salmon for those not meet eater
add estimate two drinks per person, either white, red wine, or beer.
Also, consider that we will sponsor the parking for our guests.

The event will take place on October 8th from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM. For the presentation, we will bring a large LED
screen and sound, so we only need a microphone to carry out the presentation.
Do you have inhouse ballroom microphone?

Waiting for your kind response, and I remaining at your service.

Jorge Gamboa Patrón
reviews.author: Jorge Gamboa Patrón

reviews.text: Great resort. Spacious, excellent service and high end. Very comfortable. Golf course is great and location is perfect. That said, every single restaurant on site is somewhere between mediocre and terrible. Eat anywhere off property and stay here, you'll be happy.
reviews.author: Tyler W.

reviews.text:
Phenomenal Phoenician! I had Dreamed of staying here and yes, my Dream came True!
Douglas, the Front Desk Manager was instrumental in making this Dream of mine so extraordinary! He went above and beyond to make sure that my stay was phenomenal! I highly recommend The Phoenician! The setting is Awe Inspiring! The Pools are lovely. Kevin will take good care of poolgoers! The Breakfast Buffet was Delicious with many yummy choices and excellent service by Felix and Raphael! The Dining is superb. Be sure to go to J&G Steakhouse. The manager, Kyle will make sure that your Dining experience is Magical!
reviews.author: irene eason

reviews.text: Thoroughly enjoyed my time. An actual resort, with things to do and different restaurants no need to leave if you are so inclined. The staff was fire, seeing to every need and going out of their way to help. Rooms seemed updated, new bedding. Lots of family activities. Restaurants were amazing and not overpriced. The only thing I didn't like is the landscaping needs some updating. Old turf, and walkways, river was green. But would come back for sure. 5/5
reviews.author: Toby Santos

reviews.text: We loved our stay at the Phoenician and wish it was longer! Every staff member was excellent from the valet to servers to masseuse/spa staff. We loved Christine at Mowry + Kotton and Reece at the pool to name a few. The resort is beautiful and the cactus garden is not to miss! Every part of the resort felt luxurious and we can’t wait to return one day!
reviews.author: Leah Fingerman

reviews.text: The staff at the Phoenician went out of their way to provide an amazing stay for my son and I.  Special kudos to Carol at the Athletic Club who went out of her way to help me when I rolled my ankle and ensure that we were taken care of.  She was beyond amazing!  Very clean property and I just can’t get over how special we felt as guests there.  Thank you!
reviews.author: Cali Standard

reviews.text: We enjoyed our 5 night stay at the Phoenician. We were in a mountain view, fire table casita in building A, it was nice, not amazing. Building A is an excellent location, near everything. The pool food and service were 10/10, best resort pool food I have ever had! Mostly everywhere else on property was a 9/10. However, the Tavern was 3/10. The game room was fun with our 11 year old and we enjoyed the cactus garden area. We loved the Phoenician, except for our experience at the Tavern.
reviews.author: Maggie Spehr

reviews.text:
The resort is beautiful!
The staff is amazing especially the valet service. We’ll definitely be coming back.
reviews.author: D

reviews.text: Everything here is always been great. The only problem I ever had was a snotty bartender that said he wouldn’t open the bar five minutes early.
reviews.author: Julie Chandler

reviews.text:
I was amazed by how fabulous my stay was here! The property was absolutely stunning and impressively clean; the staff truly leaves no stone unturned and has attention to all the details.

The pool was gorgeous and sparkling even during the busiest hours — there was also plenty of space to spread out and relax at all the recreational areas, even during high occupancy times.

We booked the lowest grade room for cost, but were still super impressed by the space, comfy beds, and luxury details. Even though we didn't opt for a view room, we could see a palm tree and cactus placed intentionally to break up the view of the roof/building walls. Very nice touch.

The staff is very well trained and welcoming; extremely high class team, should be very proud.

Can't wait to go back!
reviews.author: Kylie Jo Schilling (Kylie Jo)

reviews.text: Really enjoyed our stay. Comfortable clean rooms, excellent service, and great location - convenient to old town Scottsdale and metro Phoenix.
reviews.author: Russ Cummings

reviews.text:
Visited Scottsdale and Stayed here with colleagues on a work trip, had a good experience( because i had no dealings directly with the hotel staff anyway) UNTIL I encountered the people st the front-desk while colleagues checked out(i had self checked out).

1. Lesson learned: If nothing was billed to your room and you self check out, before leaving Always ask to know if there were any bills charged to the room. Fortunately i asked and realized there was. The lady by name CHAYENN treated me like a liar, it’s either she’s new and inexperienced at the job OR just blatantly negatively biased towards people of African descent . I say this because a colleague(who’s caucasian) had this similar issue of wrongful billing which was resolved by these same trio without any hassle. Her manager who was right beside her had the same condescending attitude towards me. It took me involving our chaperone as they didn’t even want to hear me out. Immediately i got the chaperone involved, it was all resolved. No apologies, no remorse, nothing! And that will be the reason why i give 1 star. Otherwise, it was a great stay.

2. It’s a beautiful place, rooms are spacious and clean(quite decent). Loved the balconies and the mountain views. Lots of walking within as the rooms are far apart. The food was great.
reviews.author: Chinny

reviews.text: Broker Open at Ascent. Fabulous!
reviews.author: Coco Dixon

reviews.text: The landscaping at The Phoenician never disappoints, no matter the season!
reviews.author: Maria Munet

reviews.text:
Excellent service from every member of the Phoenician team. Literally. Everyone from the towel guy at the pool to the servers at the bars and restaurants and everyone in between.

Where it fell short for me was the quality of the rooms, in terms of upkeep. The lampshades were stained, the carpet needed a heavy duty shampooing, and the balcony furniture cushions need a run through the laundry. The housekeeping staff should wipe down the outdoor table + sweep the balcony as part of their daily visit.

The food was great at every restaurant - special shout out for the shishito peppers at the Tavern.
The buffet dinner for one of our group events was lights out great too, everybody was impressed!
reviews.author: Barbara Riley

reviews.text: The service was exceptional! The resort was top notch.

reviews.text: Amazing experience everything is fantastic I have no complaints best experience of my life

reviews.text: What can I say, stunning hotel, outstanding staff, and service, and spotless.
reviews.author: Peter C. Geibel

reviews.text: This place has been around forever, but they have somehow kept it impeccably updated. Great location up against the bluffs in Scottsdale, this is a sprawling beautiful property with well-appointed rooms, delicious food and absolutely incredible, friendly service. We were there for a work conference and the staff went out of their way to make it memorable. Highly recommended!
reviews.author: Blake Ilstrup

reviews.text:
This has been hands down the best place I have ever stayed. Everyone I encountered on the staff was polite, friendly and exceptionally professional.
The golf course is immaculate!
Today while walking around the cactus garden out back, I stumbled upon an old golf path. It appears there used to be more holes on the course. Anyway, there were some old steps leading up to old at boxes. The views at night were spectacular.
It’s super easy to access also.
Once you reach the cactus garden entrances, use the left entrance. There is a statue of a woman holding a bowl. Off to the right of the bench behind her is a palo verde tree. The old cart path is right there. The path is also accessible by entering the garden and heading right. You will eventually see the old cart path from here too.
From either way, take a left until you come to some stairs. Thats it!
reviews.author: Cater Canyon

reviews.text: This place is hands down not a luxury experience.  For the price go stay at the Biltmore or one of the other amazing resorts in the area.  I have traveled the world and stayed in luxury hotels and this place was rundown, awful service.  The "casitas" remind me of a motel 6.  Construction was going on all around.  The place was being rented for some one year old childs' birthday party and it took over the other guest's experience.  When we arrived we had noon check in on our Marriott Bonvoy app and our room wasn't ready and the manager instead of accommodating proceeded to argue with us.  Told us he could only guarantee our room by 4pm so we came back and 4pm and it still wasn't ready for another half hour.  We had to INSIST on a credit.  It was not offered despite the guarantee and our wait.  Then at the conclusion of the visit my dress was stolen (probably by housekeeping) and they have now put me in touch with their insurer who will not call me back or answer.  One bright spot the spa (which is owned by a separate entity) and DryBar are amazing.  But come enjoy them without staying there.
reviews.author: Jamie Hazlett

reviews.text: Very poor service particularly in the main restaurant & especially the pool bar. However one restaurant the Tavern is well run and does deserve a quality rating.
reviews.author: james angelo

reviews.text: Most staff were great.  Unfortunately after traveling I really needed a nap...I was awakened by a persistent staff member wanting to check the mini frig!  She actually entered the room.  Then we had arranged for late checkout and they kept knocking about 30 min before...it was frustrating.
reviews.author: Judy C

reviews.text:
Visited in 2023 for a week long family vacation with my husband and young son. We had very high expectations given the luxury marketing and at the end of the day, they missed the mark.

Pros: beautiful property, amazing pools and splash pad, fun amenities on site, including golf! Free kids meals at some restaurants.

Cons: Poor customer service at the front desk. They downgraded our room, after we paid for an upgrade. They also didn't tell us anything about the resort so we had to figure out the amenities on our own. Our room was not well maintained (dirty carpet, rusty railing, chipped flooring, etc) and trash sat outside our room for extended periods of time in the heat.

Overall it's not a 5 star resort, due to lack of customer service and maintenance. BUT if you come in with lower expectations you will probably love this place!
reviews.author: Michelle Watson

reviews.text: The golf coarse was one of the most amazing coarse in Scottsdale. The service at the restaurant was above expected.  Brittany excited expections.

reviews.text: Always a joy

reviews.text: One fun day staycation worth it ♡

reviews.text: We had great time at the spa. Great service and we had dinner at the restuarant food and service was exceptional.
reviews.author: Zahide Sezerman

reviews.text: This is not a five star resort. Needed to talk to the front desk. I tried calling down for 25 minutes with the phone just ringing & ringing. I had to go in person. We ordered room service one night. The following morning at 7:30 am someone was banging on my door asking for the plates back. Woke up my kid. Fantastic.  The next day I was with my 6 yr old daughter & she was really thirsty. Asked the bartender for some water for her at the main lobby bar & was told they don’t open for 15 minutes so no my kid couldn’t have a water while the bartender was literally filling a cup with soda water. This place is a joke.

reviews.text: I can only rate service as I have only been to the spa.  Service and amenities are amazing.  So relaxing.  Pricey... but you feel like you get every penny's worth with everything available to you.  Definitely looking to come back soon and stay in the rooms this time!
reviews.author: N.G.K. Google account

reviews.text: This is an iconic 5☆ destination resort offering a complete experience whether for total vacation or business. Golf, cafes, restaurants, spa, tennis, full workout facility, and multiple pools.  New build homes and condos overlook the golf course and surrounding, fabulous grounds. Restful retreat in perfect location.
reviews.author: Carlee P

reviews.text: I have absolutely no idea how this property is getting high reviews. I’m currently staying here as I type this review.  The rooms feel very dated- the carpet makes you want to keep your socks on at all times. Every meal we have had on property  has been bad - some of it hasn’t been edible (the kids menu - the food has been outright gross). We had a large  room the first night however it was dirty so the manager kindly offered us an upgrade…. Now in the upgraded room, which is tiny and in close proximity to a bar - beyond loud. Generally speaking this has been an unpleasant and stressful experience. For a luxury collection property- this is off brand. Definitely not a luxury experience. Absolutely do not stay here…. Or at a minimum, don’t eat. Only positive- is the employees. They are professional and kind.
reviews.author: Tracy Yorks Demarchelier

reviews.text:
What can I say? This place took my money and ruined my March break vacation with my wife and 15-month baby.
I am a Bonvoy member, and we have never had such a horrible experience; we check-in asked for an upgrade cos we have been told that our view is the roof of a building, so we got an upgrade to a contraction site view with all the noise you can imagine we had to wake up to the sound of beeping trucks and drills. That upgrade was 150 extra on top of $1300 a night,
We asked to change the room and fought for it because the staff didn't care that we paid so much and didn't want to be on a construction site. We got moved to another room, definitely not a nice room, but it got worse!!! They moved us at 4 pm, so all day, we were paying for another night without having the comfort of having a room. Finally, we got the new room, and the room beside us was a heavy weed smoker, and our baby had to sleep breathing this cos the AC vents were connected. We complained, but no one cared!
In the end, I booked another hotel that night and moved again at 4 pm. 3 days without a normal room, but paid $2800 for it + 1300 to the new room that happened to be on the same property just a suite couldn't the stuff say sir you can upgrade to our suite sorry for the inconvenience we won't charge you for the horrible experience?!

Rooms where in bad condition and we been in 2 rooms
Service is horrible
Beautiful property
Great food
Book the suites it cost the same or DONT GO!

Coming back next trip.

reviews.text: My husband and I visited the spa at the resort for our anniversary celebration, we had a couples massage.  The massage was the worst massage I’ve had in 10 years. The woman didn’t have the skill set to give a proper massage. They require to you to pay 20% for gratuity, which I would have been happy to pay if I got a worthy massage from them. We sat down for lunch in between our services and it took an hour from start to finish to get our food. We had to hurry and eat and we couldn’t enjoy some of the amenities due to their lack of service. I wouldn’t recommend spending thousands of dollars here for the spa. I’d look elsewhere.

reviews.text: Awesome place if you're rich. $550 for a couple bottles of mediocre champagne and gooseberries isn't very reasonable. Again maybe I'm not the right person to review this. It's real nice but as a normal person the prices are dumb.

reviews.text: Had the privilege of attending a conference at the hotel and couldn’t have had a better experience. During the check-in, I was greeted by Ben, who provided an exceptional experience. Recognizing my Bonvoy loyalty, despite the event booking not transferring my rewards number, and talking about amenities available at the property, he made sure I was well prepared to enjoy a great stay at the property. Our dinner at J&G was outstanding, and the property amazing throughout the stay. Thanks for a great week!
reviews.author: Matthew Benidt

reviews.text: Dino P, the bartender, doesn't tip his delivery drivers. What kind of bartender at a luxury resort doesnt tip their service? I do not recommend this person
reviews.author: Steven

reviews.text: Absolutely gorgeous property! All of the staff was so kind and extremely professional. The rooms were spacious and clean. The food was delicious. All of the shops, and restaurants, and amenities were exceptional. Highly recommend.

reviews.text: Perfect in everyway
reviews.author: Jennifer Gross

reviews.text: Went for high tea and it was so fun! The food and tea was delicious! The service was amazing and the environment was wonderful.
reviews.author: Maddi Johnson

reviews.text:
The property is beautiful. The rooms are not. At least, mine was not. Broken fixtures. Holes in the wall. Paint splatters on the floors. Light fixtures from 30 years ago (fluorescent tubes that hum). Clogged sinks. Stains in the carpet. Old (pre smart tv) tech. One of the sets of drapes were stuck and wouldn’t open.

Other little things like the tons of construction everywhere and the fact that I tried the basketball courts and the basketballs were all tore up all added up to an experience that was just not on par.

Look at my review history and you’ll see that I don’t leave a ton of negative reviews.

It wasn’t “bad” by all hotel standards, but by $1800/night standards, it’s totally unacceptable.

If they remodeled it, then it absolutely could be worth the rate.

As it stands, there is no chance I would recommend the hotel if you want to have an upscale experience.

The resort has potential, but either I was in the lowest quality room on the property (the “executive suite”), or the standards for the rooms themselves are super low for any Marriott.

To be fair, I didn’t pay for it (it was paid for by someone else) - but I have spent a lot of time in a lot of Marriott hotels.
reviews.author: Daniel Englebretson

reviews.text: Beautiful scenery and wonderful accommodation.  All except for the 2 Valet gentlemen. They were rude and smelt like they had been smoking. While I was waiting for my rideshare driver to pick me up, they wouldn't let me wait inside out of the heat.

Breakfasts were outstanding and the service is one of the best we’ve experienced; every single staffer was polite and helpful over the top. Tim at the Mowry and Cotton restaurant was exceptionally helpful and friendly. Expensive, yes; but in this case you definitely get what you pay for!

reviews.text: It's very hard to fault a place with such a great reputation and The Phoenician certainly knows how to roll-out the red carpet. But if there were one little gripe I have it's that it feels a little contrived - that or the staff is just over it. No matter, this place, for the money, is WORTH IT!

reviews.text: Top notch hotel and service. Was here for a conference for a few days. Grounds and staff are exceptional.
reviews.author: Doug

reviews.text:
Stayed here for the long weekend with my husband and 11 month old baby. The location and overall hotel were beautiful but the service left a lot to be desired. On the reservation we listed a need for a crib, my husband called twice prior to the reservation date and on the morning of, and when I checked in I requested a crib. I got to the room needing to put my overtired baby down for a nap. I proceeded to wait *two* more hours (involving two more phone calls) for a crib to arrive; by this point my baby was miserable and it took another hour to get him down for a nap.

We self parked, on the second day, we realized the A elevator in the parking garage lobby was broken. Their elevator system won’t let you summon a different elevator. So, we had to bring our baby in a stroller on the escalator. Imagine if someone in a wheelchair had needed to get upstairs (I’m fairly certain this was an ADA violation). If you’re going to get that kind of elevator system, you better make sure it works.

We needed another comforter; 6 hours later it wasn’t there. The TV chromecast function didn't work. The Parking Garage didn’t work with the room keys.

Overall, this was a disappointing visit. Lovely area and hotel from the outside, but I’ve gotten better, more attentive service at a Best Western.
reviews.author: Hannah Rooney

reviews.text: Incredible atmosphere
reviews.author: Ryan Henderson

reviews.text: Afternoon tea was very nice as always. Server was a little slow.

reviews.text: Presentation of Vivaldi 's Four Seasons,  excellent concert.

reviews.text:
This place probably was 5 star forty years ago. But now it’s old, outdated and worn out. From the scary dirty parking garage to the run down lobby areas, it looks rough. (See photos) Broken floor tiles, cracked glass doors, finishes from decades ago. I’ve stayed at actual 5 star resorts and this is NOT. It looks like they have unable to afford maintenance and updates for many years. Which is surprising considering their insane rates!

Anyways our stay was booked with a discounted rate. So they stuck us in a room with the view literally being a stucco wall directly outside of the window lol! We could see ac thin slice of the sky above the wall. It was really unbelievable. We started laughing when we opened the shades. It’s not really the kind of room anyone should pay money for. It would make a good storage room. Oh and the bathroom has industrial T-bar ceiling. Like the kind at the DMV. This is the mentality of the owners. And that’s who has decided not to maintain the property for decades.

There are so many nice new modern resorts. Don’t waste your time at this run down dinosaur lol
reviews.author: Man N

reviews.text:
This review has nothing to do with the room quality or amenities or facilities, those are all quite nice and frankly should be for the nightly rate you are paying. This review ties directly to the staff and their lack of care for their guests.

We were there for a weekend with family and friends attending a wedding. On the day of the wedding my wife went to the pool for one hour by herself. She got her towels and set her things down on a chair. She then received a phone call that she took and spoke for 15 minutes next to the pool with her back turned to the chair. At this time someone grabbed all of her things including her purse and sandals. This pool probably had 20 guests at the pool at this time, not a lot of activity. All the staff had the same lethargic response, “I am sorry mam, there is nothing we can do.”

Now let me be crystal clear, we are not ascribing blame directly to the hotel. They certainly cannot be responsible for all guests' belongings at all times and my wife made a costly error in judgment, although an unconscious one, she never should have turned her back to her items.

We immediately shut down credit cards but saw that the culprit already tried to charge $1,500 at Neiman Marcus just down the street so now we had validation that this was no accident or misplaced items. One gentleman who worked at the front desk (I wish I had his name) even had the nerve to tell us, “Things get stolen from the pool all the time” - If that statement is true, maybe an examination of security protocols might be a priority.

Rather than attend our wedding we spent the reception filling out a police report. We knew the chances of recovery were slim and the financial loss was significant (>$500) but not catastrophic. The point is there is an absolute dearth of security at this resort. I can’t list all the shortcomings but here are a few: There are no cameras anywhere on the three pool decks (at least that is what we were told), All gates to the pools remain wide open at all times. I have stayed at resorts who charge half as much as the phonecian and they still require a room key to access the pools. The parking lot entry attendant showed no enforcement as far as which cars were allowed on property.

Here is the kicker. 7 hours after the purse was first stolen another charge was attempted on our canceled credit card BACK ON THE PHOENICIAN property. We thought this was our chance, how many establishments are even open at 10 PM to accept payment on the property? We alerted hotel management immediately and again the blank stares, the nonchalance, complete and utter deflection, “I am sorry, we can’t track that.” How easy would it have been upon our initial claim to tell their staff “If you run a credit card that is denied then alert security immediately.” With today’s tech and ubiquitous communication that is such an easy catch. You would think at $700/night there might be a modicum of effort or assistance for their guests.

Moral of the Story: Don’t take anything valuable to the pool and Don’t rely on the staff. Their customer service extends as far as reading a script, over and over again. They are sorry, but there is nothing they can do, ahem, willing to do.

(11/15 Follow up to Mr. Fredricks response)
With all due respect Ben, I find it a bit disingenuous to be told I am getting a “response from the business owner” when in reality it is a room operations manager who has been in the workforce for just over six years. I don’t mean to slight you directly Ben, you could be highly proficient at your role and I know this lack of attention to our case is not orchestrated by you. The frustration is with your bosses who are merely applying damage control. It is a strategy as old as time, deflect and neglect. Placate the upset client with feckless apologies in hopes they just go away. You allude to hints of action, “steps are being taken“ . . .

Please feel free to contact us with what exactly these are. We accept your “sincere apologies” but six weeks later, we are awaiting to see what these might be.

reviews.text:
I was invited to a private cocktail hour by the sponsor of the conference I am attending. I am a black woman and I arrived with my colleagues who are black and Hispanic. We arrived to the happy hour and spoke to the host. We mingled and said hello to a few attendees. One we sat down and looked over the menu, a waitress came over to take our order. She asked me for my card to start a tab. I thought this was odd because it was a private cocktail event and the host was paying for everything. I gave her my card. I checked in with another attendee and asked if we were paying for our drinks and food. They told me no. When the waitress returned I told her that I was a part of the private event and she said "Oh, someone told me that you all snuck into the back of this event and you're not with them." She politely returned my card, however, that doesn't change the racial bias that I experienced at the hands of this hotel.

Before taking our initial order she could've asked if we were a part of private event. She could've asked the host. Yet, instead she chose to believe something the "someone" told her. These are microagressions. There was a lack of respect for me because if it was a private event and I want not meant to be in that area, she could've asked me to move. This is how racism persists because two black people and a Hispanic person look like they don't belong at an upscale event at a luxury hotel. My night was soured and my experience at this hotel event as an invited guest was ruined.
reviews.author: Jessica Hortman

reviews.text:
Overall nothing but great things to say about this place. Great location, great service, incredible pool area, etc. We even were able to get a free upgrade using Suite Night awards from our Marriott status which was an incredible perk. I would highly recommend The Phoenician.

I would share a few complaints however. First and foremost, if you eat at the onsite restaurant Mowry & Cotton make sure you keep your receipt. I did not keep my receipt for one of our meals there and was over charged by close to $100. To date, no one from the restaurant has been willing to help me get the dispute resolved nor have they been able to provide a copy of the receipt showing the charges that I actually signed for.

Only other complaint is related to the pool area. Overall, the pool area is awesome. However, the water was pretty dirty in both pools we used. There was a dirt line around the top of the water level and there was a good bit of bird poop in the bottom of the pools. The adult only pool was closed for most of our stay which was a bummer.

I would definitely visit the Phoenician again, but will be staying away from Mowry and Cotton restaurant during my next stay unless someone can actually get the overbill resolved.

reviews.text:
Imposantes Haus aus den 80igern, das seinen Special Touch noch nicht verloren hat. Das Hotel ist eine Destinationen für sich.

Anreise: In Scottsdale gelegen ist es circa 30 Minuten vom Flughafen. Circa 10 Minuten mit dem Auto zur Fashion Square Mall und zu Old Town Scottsdale Imposante (nicht kontrollierte) Einfahrt, die entlang der Ferienwohnungen und am Golfplatz und am Fitnesskomplex vorbei dann letztendlich im eigentlichen Hotel mündet.

Auf dem Weg zum Hotel passiert man die Canyon Suites. Eigenes Gebäude mit eigenen Empfang und eigenem Pool, etwas teurer. Wir hatten uns dort die Räumlichkeiten zeigen lassen, hatten aber nicht den Eindruck, dass sich der Aufpreis tatsächlich in der Qualität der Räumlichkeiten widerspiegelt, da man im eigentlichen Hotel ohnehin schon auf extrem hohen Niveau ist.
Allerdings ist bei den Canyon Suites (es gibt dort auch „normale“ Zimmer) das Frühstück bereits inbegriffen. Die Poollandschaft des Haupthauses kann man natürlich mit benutzen.

Check In: imposante Vorfahrt mit regionaler Kunst, gespickt. Freundliche Begrüßung durch die Valets, die sofort das Gepäck Aufnahmen und es Richtung Lobby brachten. Check In verlief freundlich und reibungslos. Leider keine kleine Aufmerksamkeit für Kinder. Karte als Überblick wurde ausgehändigt. Guter Concierge Desk.

Die Lobby selbst wird von großen Panoramafenstern und mittiger Bar bestimmt. Lebhafte Lobby zum verweilen.

Zimmer: Zimmer über vier Etagen. Lobby selbst ist im 3. OG. Erst ab Deluxe Pool View hat man einen wirklich schönen Blick. Ansonsten gehen die Zimmer Richtung Hotel - Vorfahrt oder Richtung Berge.

Sehr große Zimmer, mit Sitzecke und großem bestuhlten Balkon. Nicht mehr ganz taufrisch, gut funktionierende Klimaanlage, Kaffeemaschine mit Pads, großes Bad, mit separater Dusche und Badewanne. Viele Ablagemöglichkeiten gut beleuchtet.

Pools/Spa/Fitness: wirklich schöne Pool Landschaft über drei Stufen. Davon ein Pool, nur für Erwachsene; sehr angenehme Wasser Temperaturen. Ausreichend Liegen mit Sonnenschirmen. Weiche Auflagen. Schnelle Wasserrutsche für die Kids + Splash Pad. Sehr großzügig gestaltet. Hinter den Pool befindet sich dann das separates Spa Gebäude und dahinter der Golfclub.
Fitnessclub für ein Hotel auf Weltklasse Niveau. 24 Stunden. Alles neu!

Für Kids: wie gesagt, große Poollandschaft und Wasserrutsche ist ein Highlight für alle Kids. Zudem gibt es einen großen, mit zahlreichen Videospielen ausgestatteten Game Room unterhalb des Fitness Centers.

Auch wird ein KidsClub angeboten. Allerdings wirkt dieser wenig ansprechen und die Aktivitäten kosten zusätzlich und sind limitiert. Das ginge bei solch ein Luxusadresse sicherlich besser .

Essen: tolles Fleisch im Steakhouse J&G im Obergeschoss. Ansonsten gibt es noch einen Coffee Shop mit gutem Frühstück und frischen Lunch. Lobby mit Snacks. Das Restaurant im Golfclub haben wir nicht besucht. Das Gartenrestaurant war leider geschlossen Mowry&Cotton.

Personal: besonders gut bei Valet und Concierge. Front Desk, mal so mal so. Housekeeping top! Restaurants: das geht besser - J&G unorganisiert.

Fazit: beeindruckendes Luxus-Haus mit toller Poollandschaft und exzellentem Fitness Club. Zimmer könnten einen Refresh vertragen. Personal mal so mal so. Bei Kindern könnte man sich etwas mehr Mühe geben.

Our stay at the iconic Phoenician could not have been better. Though I was hesitant to visit in the heat of the off-season, everything at this property ended up exceeding expectations. Over the course of six days, we sampled the various onsite restaurants and bars, as well as the spa, pools, and health club. The staff are friendly and personable, and we got to know the bartenders at both J&G and the Thirsty Camel quite well - who were quick to remember our names and preferences. The spa experience was among the best anywhere, and the room itself was luxurious and well-appointed with a spacious patio.
Service requests could perhaps be addressed a bit faster, but for the most part our experience was flawless. I’m reminded again why I continually place my trust in the Luxury Collection portfolio.

reviews.text:
I guess I was expecting more for a $400+ a night resort. The rooms were nice and comfortable and certainly spacious. Had issues with the minibar fridge from day one. Wouldn't close properly, so drinks were not as cold. Brought it to the resorts attention but never got taken care of. Love that the pools are open 24/7 because that heat was brutal 115 to 119 during the day.
The gym is spectacular with modern equipment that works. There are two blink charging stations inside the parking garage. Cost at the time was .49c a kwH. That was a huge plus!
The kids' activities are good and happy they offer them. Unfortunately, I didn't have the opportunity to try the spa, but it certainly looked upscale and nice! One inconvenience was walking to the pool from our room. It certainly took a bit of a walk and had to pass multiple places to get to it. Honestly, I'm not sure if I'd go again.
reviews.author: Ivan D

reviews.text: Wake up to an amazing breakfast and help staff that will recommend the best mimosa pairing. The room are spectacular but don’t waste time in your room when you have several different pools to lazy around in. After a lazy day get ready for live entertainment from dueling pianos, live bands …
reviews.author: Nash McGee

reviews.text: I did not stay, I met a friend there. It's just beautiful. The service is excellent 💯
reviews.author: Lisa Reyes

reviews.text: Love this place. Pools are wonderful. Rooms large
reviews.author: Debbie Soprano

reviews.text: Fantastic resort.  Impeccable, kid-friendly service.  We will be back!
reviews.author: JD Murdock

reviews.text: I’m not a complainer especially as I am traveling with friends for their birthday. I honestly was disappointed with the fact that this resort was 5 stars and was not even comparable to the Hilton Resorts and Hotels I’ve stayed at. I was not impressed with the service and also the restaurants. The resort seemed a bit ran down and needs to be updated. For the price that was paid, it was disappointing. The front desk staff was rude and cold. The pool staff I can honestly say we’re more warm and welcoming. Also the housekeeping staff is amazing. But front desk staff especially during 2nd shift is unbearable. I try to be very understanding and nice as possible. Especially because this Arizona heat is  out of this world, but the service for the front staff for amenities was super slow. Asked for some toothbrushes around 8pm and didn’t get them until around midnight… by that time we all fell asleep and was not going to answer the door. It was a bit rude. Then came the day I ordered doordash and the dasher ends up sending it to the front desk. Told me it would be a $5 charge which is understandable to deliver it to my casita. Did not get my food until two phone calls and a whole hour later. Both times I called the front desk rep was cold and hung up after she told me she was going to send it. I ended up telling her to throw it away as I didn’t have a way to reheat my food. She rudely told me she will send it again and hung up. Then when it was delivered, no one ever knocked on the door. Got a call from the front desk that it was delivered and she hung up again rudely. Just providing some feedback as I usually don’t stay at Marriot properties but was excited that I was invited on vacation with my friends to this “amazing resort”. I say don’t waste your money. This pregnant woman aka me was not happy what so ever. I will make sure I stay at the Waldorf or the W next time when I visit myself.
reviews.author: Christina Nguyen

reviews.text: I was there for a business conference.  The room was big and beautiful, very comfortable.  We enjoyed the J&G Steakhouse 2 nights in a row.  The bar on the main level was great with an awesome view.  They provided very tasty snacks with our drinks. The conference rooms were very comfortable. The food provided by the resort for our conference was surprisingly very good.
reviews.author: Suzanne Hessman

reviews.text: Terrible service  and front desk ver dismissive
reviews.author: monica pereira

reviews.text:
It’s a cool location and huge. But the resort itself is old and super dirty. The first room they gave us was infested with moths. They switched our room both rooms was sooo dusty and had spiderwebs in the corners and on the curtains. Carpets had stains on them as well. It appeared that no one had visually inspected these rooms in months.
Hallways were also super dusty and had Beatles and roaches walking through it.
For what we paid we expected a lot nicer and way cleaner. Super disappointing.
reviews.author: Darrell B

reviews.text: Beautiful Property just confusing once you get to the parking
reviews.author: Lexx With 2 X's

reviews.text: The hotel is fantastic with a three-story spa, and fitness center. It is where the 1987 movie starring Nicolas Cage, Holly Hunter, Frances McDormand "Raising Arizona" was filmed. It is in my book "Arizona's Historic and Unique Hotels". Dr. Diane Holloway Cheney.
