reviews.text: Great resort; schedule should have been provided on check-in, check-in staff seemed bewildered; wonderful kids activities ~ kids activity staff: superb, kind, high energy, upbeat and positive! ; room decor slightly dated (in the casitas); "The Resort Shop" staff: bovine, condescending ~ prices (for spray-on sunscreen $28 and sunscreen chapstick $8), shockingly exorbitant, disappointing ~ hotel revenue opportunity: yes, hotel reputation damage: not insignificant; walk up upper pool bar 'Kalio' service, awful; but (only 75ft away) the walk up middle pool bar service (by Alex) over three days, wonderful!; housekeeping service, superb!; parking staff, terrific professionals (thank you Kevin!); dining: Mowry & Cotton breakfast buffet, best in the business!

The property is beautiful from the lobby bar to the rooms, to the amazing pools, there is a place for everyone. The staff is extremely helpful. After speaking with a number of them, I found out that many have long tenures at the property. It shows. Everyone is extremely knowledgeable. Can’t wait to return!

reviews.text: An excellent destination resort for a golfing adventure or a business event. The staff is extremely attentive to your needs. The food is great, and the facilities and amenities are amazing.
reviews.author: Rick Komas (TinyStudio)

reviews.text: By far the best resort in the valley. First class all the way. Don't forget to checkout the garden in back of the resort.
reviews.author: Kirk Thompson

reviews.text: Very nice 5 star hotel. Poolside food service, top notch restaurants, on site breakfast shop and souvenir shops. And the view of camel back mountain at sunset with the one you love, what more could you ask for. Also very kid friendly, they even have a pool with waterside
reviews.author: R P

reviews.text: I recently stayed the phoenician for a business trip. I have traveled to Arizona almost every year of my life and I have always wanted to stay at the phoenician. Overall, I was happy with my stay. I will start off with the bad. The shower pressure was very high and although the shower got hot, the pressure sometimes made it feel like you were getting hosed down. It was fine to get clean, but it was not a very relaxing shower. Also, there were so many bugs in the room. I was not in the room much because of work, I saw grasshoppers in my room on 4 different times. I killed 2 of them so there were at least 3 grasshoppers in my room possibly more. It did make my stay slightly uncomfortable. I told the front desk, but they said there was nothing they could do. I was able to deal with it for my stay but I would not have wanted to spend another night in that room because of the bugs.  For the good, the bathroom was huge with a nice tub The gym was nice and the hotel has excellent service from the valet, to housekeeping and front desk. Overall, I my experience was a 3 out of 5 mainly because of the bugs. If I didn't experience that, I would give my experience a 4.5.
reviews.author: Jeremy Goodwin

reviews.text: This is a beautiful resort, with excellent & very comfortable rooms. The food at all the restaurants is fantastic. The customer service was 5 star. They attended to your every need and special thanks to Reggie and Dakota for always going above and beyond to make our stay as superb as possible.
reviews.author: Frank Ivancic (IDM)

reviews.text:
We booked a small "staycation" as we live in the Phoenix area and wanted to experience some of Marriott's local offerings.

Already aware of the resort's architectural significance, we had high expectations. Our experience did not disappoint!

The resort does a great job recognizing Marriott Bonvoy status and providing perks. Check-in was smooth. Room was exceptional as we walked in. The bathrooms are VERY spacious and well-designed. Rooms are very quiet with great views. The resort looks incredible at all times of the day and is truly special to look at. Very clean room and balcony.

Room service offered a great experience. The gentleman that took our order was thorough and repeated it back. The gentleman that delivered our food set the table and created conversation with us. The grilled club was delicious, and the cheesecake was a great dessert. Presentation was spot on.

The property was great to walk around and explore, with just about any offering you may want at a resort.

The only area of improvement I noticed was signage to self-parking. It wasn't necessarily obscure, but easy to pass up. We noticed it when we looped back around.

We will definitely be returning for additional stays in the future!
reviews.author: Aaron Gelarden

reviews.text: Beautiful resort which a gorgeous pool! I had a great stay. Make sure to stop by MOWRY & COTTON and visit my favorite bartender Jordan! He makes the best drinks 😃
reviews.author: Ashley

reviews.text: Service from all employees was great! Thought the pool was a bit warm of June (only 100⁰ out)
reviews.author: Stevi Weaver

reviews.text: An experience everyone should enjoy.
reviews.author: Lou Linares

reviews.text: Great golf course, greens not perfect but everything else was spot on.
reviews.author: Aimee Pyatt

reviews.text: Hotel property is beautiful- service top notch, I would have given 5 stars, but rooms need a little maintenance
reviews.author: Jason Trefanenko

reviews.text:
Our family of 6 stayed at this resort last week. When we normally check into a Marriott, we are usually warmly welcomed and thanked for our Titanium Elite status. When we pulled up to this "luxury collection" resort, we waited in a long line to check in and then we were offered upgraded rooms, then asked to pay an extra $250 per night for them. We have NEVER, in 20 years of being Elite guests, been asked to pay for an upgrade. If they are available, they should be offered to Titanium Elite members as a complimentary benefit of our status.

The rooms were big, one had a nice view of the mountain and the other looked at the roof of another building. The main pool was closed for an undisclosed amount of time, leaving only two overly crowded pools for our entire stay. Our umbrella flew out of our umbrella holder and landed in the pool, luckily not injuring anyone, but spilling water all over my phone and ruining the speakers. Why are these not more securely fastened?

For a luxury resort, I found it distasteful to host two large corporate conventions at the same time. People were constantly scatted about the hotel taking business calls, having meetings and networking. Even by the pool and spa. It felt less like I was at a luxury resort and more like I was at a WeWork. The entire time it made me feel like I had to check my email...hard to disconnect from the real world when everywhere you look you're reminded of it. Not to mention, a couple of days one of the pool was closed off to only members of the company outing...why did management think it was smart to do this when you're already down one pool? They must value companies' checkbooks more than loyal guests who pay a lot of their own money to stay there.

Tennis and Pickleball were good, the spa was way too crowded and the bikes and golf were fine.

The last thing and maybe the most important...stop advertising your hotel as a 5-star hotel when only a part of it is. If you want to stay at a 5-star hotel, you need to book at the Canyon Suites building of the Phoenician. The rest of the Phoenician is about a 3.5-star convention center.
reviews.author: L H

reviews.text: This hotel is in major need of maintenance and customer service. The first issue I had was the toilet seat was broken. It took them 3 hours to come and fix it as the front desk stated they had numerous maintenance calls. I didn't get that resolved until almost 2am. The next issue is their shower was broken. Water barely came out, which is not the worst part of it. The worst part is the fact that they had a loose handle and the screw was so loose that it came out. I almost stepped on a screw while I was showering at a 5 diamond hotel. This place should be no more than a 2 diamond. Lastly, I visited their pool in the evening to notice that everyone had maintenance issues. There was tile missing everywhere and the areas it was missing, the objects were sharp. I came close to cutting myself several times against the wall so I left the pool area. AAA and Forbes, you need to revisit this place and downgrade them.
reviews.author: Brett Sapowith

reviews.text: We visited the Thirsty Camel for cocktails on a Thursday evening and we loved it! The live music was terrific, the views breathtaking, and the drinks and appetizers so yummy!
reviews.author: Laura Barbera

reviews.text: Beautiful Hotel by far the nicest I have ever been to. Gorgeous scenery.
reviews.author: Kody Townsend

reviews.text: I loved everything about this property. The grounds and views are stunning. Everyone had such a great attitude and was willing to help. The pool was warm however some leafs and debris was on there so we stayed out. Not season yet.

reviews.text: The High Tea at The Phoenician is so lovely. Having high tea at the Phoenician is a family tradition that spans more than two decades and three generations. It never disappoints, and I can't wait to introduce my grandsons to this much loved tradition.

reviews.text: Beautiful resort with multiple pools including adult only pools. Pool side Cabanas are available for rent (very reasonable price), pool side service for drinks and food was excellent. Highly recommend staying here.

reviews.text: Visited Mowry and Cotton for brunch. Very upscale resort with restaurant to match. Food and drinks were great, and they were excellent service.

reviews.text: This was a nice resort and the level of service was incredibly high. Every staff member I interacted with was pleasant and friendly. Big shout out to the servers working the adult pool, there was a large group of us and they were a great blend of fun and professionalism.

reviews.text: Love staying here with my husband great experience

reviews.text: I am a trucker and I was in that place to load my truck. They have a work team in the truck loading and unloading area that is very very friendly. They are very fast and professional in their work. They offered lunch to me and to another trucker who was also there. There, it is the first time that a business has this detail with me and I have been a truck driver for several years, I recommend this place, and I am very grateful to your work team
reviews.author: Angel cule

reviews.text: Best place for relaxation at the spa and beautiful ground for a vacay!!
reviews.author: Dorrell Edwards

reviews.text: Just ok. There are “yes” 5 star resorts and “no” star resorts and this one is definitely a “no”. Staff does not attempt to add to the luxury experience from a service perspective, and are very quick to tell you “those are the rules” or “that’s not our policy” for even very simple requests. Unlike all other 5 stars I have been to, at this hotel you can expect to set up your own pool chairs with towels and chase down wait staff for service (with items often forgotten multiple times). No extra touches like most 5 stars such as warm or cool towels and/or a welcome drink on arrival. No greeting by name like at the other 5 stars as well. Just felt like a regular Marriott with minimal effort, and slightly nicer rooms, common spaces, and grounds. Pool area definitely felt like a Holiday Inn - it was not beautiful and I did not enjoy the ambiance while sitting at it. Food was also just ok - presentation nice enough and it was overall good but nothing to write home about. Meh. If you do chose to stay here, don’t miss the cactus garden - the best part of the hotel! The spa was also beautiful but our experience was tainted by unprofessional staff. We would not stay again and considered moving to the Arizona Biltmore halfway through but we were with family and so we stayed.  The only thing 5 star about this place was the room price.
reviews.author: Patricia Frey

reviews.text: We always have a great time at The Canyon Suites. The suites are huge and well laid out, the grounds are beautiful and the staff is on point.
reviews.author: Bill Sutherland

reviews.text: Phoenician was a disappointment. As a positive, the food was good and the cactus garden and golf course are really beautiful. However, the rooms are drab and depressing which is surprising for a $1k a night room. The pools and kids areas are old and need to be remodeled. They don’t have house keeping unless you specifically request it and our hot water didn’t work the last night. We switched to the JW Marriott which is much better.  The Phoenician is definitely not a 5 star hotel by any means so if you’re looking  for that quality look elsewhere.
reviews.author: L Golden

reviews.text: Stayed in the three bedroom residence. At first impression we were very happy, but as we began to explore I was horrified at the living area couch. For a stay at $2k per night, this is unacceptable. I am a lifetime titanium elite member and have stayed in A LOT of Marriott properties. This was the most disappointed I’ve ever been. Check out the pics I attached. The icing on the cake, my wife got food poisoning! Spoke to front desk and they handed me off to the head of security? Never got a call from F & B manager. Guess this person could care less of the level of food handling in his department. Had to finally call the front desk manager at the end of the day to express grief. She was very nice and gave a $500 bill credit. I don’t ever complain at hotels and having traveled as much as I do, don’t make a big deal out of things, but comping a nights stay would have been more in line. Especially considering my poor wife was bed ridden all day and the inability to use the couch. We won’t be back. What a joke.
reviews.author: David Brown

reviews.text: Went to a great pickleball clinic at the Phoenician this past Monday!

reviews.text: A marvelous place that has been around for a while and still maintains a high level of quality

reviews.text:
Service, grounds, and food was fabulous.
Room felt like they were trying make a rough room feel luxury in the casitas. The door alone we had to slam to close. The spa was lovely except my massage started 5 minutes late and ended 5 minutes early and I didn’t get the add-on I paid for. Note that the spa also tacks on service charges on top of your spa package. I didn’t want to complain in front of other guests so I gave them feedback afterwards and the spa didn’t reply or make it right.

reviews.text:

reviews.text: Currently staying on resort. I wouldn’t stay here again. There are way better options in the valley that would live up to the expectations tied to the price paid. From having the pool boy drop a tray full of food on us pool side, when asking about cleaning off items getting attitude from the pool  boy. He brought over a manager to have us clean our own stuff and then finally apologized. To not having items available that are in the menu. Our view is over taken by construction going on. We had a house keeper enter our room once unannounced after cleaning our room, she quickly handed me some hand towels as if we requested them and left, 10 minutes later she tried to come back into our room again asking about her iPad that was not in our room and I would not let her in. From that point on we have been locking up our belongings in the safe as if this was a motel 6. 1/10 would not recommend.

reviews.text:
This review is specifically for the Afternoon Tea:

A couple of friends and I have been making it a point to check out every afternoon tea there is in the area - this one takes the cake. The resort is just beautiful and afternoon tea is served in the front dining area with a gorgeous view and a live pianist. Our servers were lovely and really went above and beyond to ensure we enjoyed ourselves. We treated ourselves to the Grand Royal Tea, which is full tea plus champagne. Our glasses were never empty, and our tea pots always full. The finger sandwiches were delicious and we adored our little sweets which were so carefully decorated and plated - just beautiful!

Thank you so much for making this such a great experience for us and setting the standard for a high tea. Will definitely be back again!
reviews.author: Olivia Cline

reviews.text: We stayed in the firetable king casita Mountain View room and it’s one of the best rooms available. I don’t know how I could describe my experience in words but long story short my stay here was not long enough. Peaceful vibes with a true resort feel. Golf, dine, relax, and catch some Zzz’s in luxury ;)

reviews.text: Phoenix Area Legend!  Cheers!  JMAC

reviews.text: Wow, just entering the property and driving to the luxurious lobby is a real treat. It was dark when I arrived and as I pulled up my car turned into a Bently stretch limo and I, into a princess arriving to a ball in my honor. Everyone was waiting to greet me, just hoping for a chance to make eye contact with me. Upon my departure, much to my despair, I returned to the white trash that I was before my arrival. However, my time spent in the lap of ultimate luxury will not soon be forgotten.
reviews.author: Josh Kennison

reviews.text: We recently visited the Phoenician for the 4th time for a girl's trip. This is a place we continue to come though it's not perfect. The spa is perfection though - every time it is just simply a day out of heaven. The spa pool could have better service - but they made it right for us, so won't say too much. The room is not really anything to write home about. It's clean but it does feel a little old and outdated and there are some non-luxury things like little stains on the carpet, chips in the furniture, etc. I really wish they would put real doors on the bathroom. Especially when you are with friends - there is no privacy to be able to use the restroom facilities. You can hear everything and there are large cracks between the shutter doors so you really don't feel like you can relax when you are showering or going to the bathroom. Maybe add a fan for noise privacy? The bathroom was mostly clean and can't really complain. You must request a room with a view - the resort view is everything! So gorgeous to sit off your balcony and look at the resort. The pools and grounds are simply amazing and the views of Camelback Mountain just can't be beat. While it's not perfect, we love going and will go again.

reviews.text: Just beautiful

Our room provided a top-floor city view where we could see the Phoenix skyline. All of the staff we interacted with were pleasant from the front desk and valet to housekeeping and restaurant staff. We unfortunately arrived on a not-so-great weather weekend so we didn’t get to take advantage of the pool or sports activities. The resort is located off Camelback road making an easy trip to wherever you may be headed.

reviews.text: Absolutely lovely resort and great staff!

reviews.text: The property has an extremely large foot print. We were in an extremely nice Executive King Suite very spacious. Room was at the end of the hallway it's a walk. I would of rather stayed by the pool very beautiful views. Should you visit make a full day after working out in their amazing fitness room then head to the spa. Relax in the steam room, hot tub, and saun before get spa services. I got a hydro facial and a wonderful message.  So relaxing your sure to fall asleep. Everyone through out the property was so helpful. Would visit again preferably in the summer to enjoy the pool.
reviews.author: Sugar

reviews.text:
I booked this resort specifically to have access to the spa. I like to enjoy a nice steam/sauna and to relax. My wife likes to get massages and facials.

Upon arrival after our first night I was told by the spa I could not access the facility without having a service. I was told they were fully booked and I couldn’t even pay to access the spa facilities.

I’ve never stayed at a luxury resort and been denied access to the spa facilities as a guest on the property.

I requested a refund and promptly booked a room at The Sanctuary.

I will never stay at this hotel again. I wasn’t even offered a refund or complimentary anything for the inconvenience.

I highly recommend never staying here. You can’t even use all the facilities yet pay a premium for access to the grounds?
reviews.author: Chris DeLong

reviews.text:
I would return to this hotel. Why?
Rooms were generous and well appointed, but dated.
Room and Concierge Service were excellent.
The grounds are lovely and the pool fun for kids and adults alike.
Everything food related is very very average, and really not up to par with the rest of the place. The pool restaurant and breakfast place has a menu 1980 style, ingredients are poor, salads over sauced and salty, sandwiches fatty and unhealthy, coffee is school cafeteria level. Lobby bar serves cheese plate , samosas, etc of a quality like you get in an economy flight.
Pool food same issue. By car good alternatives are close.
Besides the food we would go back.
reviews.author: l. b.

reviews.text: The property, the golf, the spa, the restaurants were all better than what we had hoped for but what really set this place apart was the people.  Will, Joyce, Chef Boyer, Ireland, Chase and I could go on.  Every employee we came into contact with was first class and always willing to help to assure we were taken care of.  I would highly recommend the Canyon Suites to any and all.  Thanks for a great stay!

reviews.text: The resort was beautiful the pools were heated the room was clean not elaborate but nice the restaurants were very pricey and the food was okay overall the stay was good

reviews.text: Really nice hotel with beautiful views.

reviews.text: I couldn’t wait to be wowed by the luxury but I guess I will keep waiting. The grounds are stunning. The entrance is impressive. It goes downhill from there. The lobby has a smell being pumped into it that reminds me of the smell of bowling shoe spray. The rooms are nice but they are a nice Marriott room. I would not go so far as to call it luxury. Luxury doesn’t have chips in the furniture and paint. The lamps aren’t crooked. The bathroom doors close completely. Maybe the golf and tennis make up for it but the room and food DO NOT. $115 for stale chips, super vinegary wings, extremely watery blue cheese. Or how about $50 for a piece of toast. And it irritates me that my mini bar is stocked with Pepsi. Not a Coke anywhere! The staff are extremely nice and prompt so I do give them points for that. Courtney was the BEST server!

reviews.text: We have been coming to Holiday tea at the Phoenician for over 20 years and this is the first time I was truly disappointed in the food. They replaced their egg salad sandwich with a pickled deviled egg that tasted like a shot of apple cider vinegar. They also replaced the roast beef sandwich with a "lobster roll" which tasted like a cheap California roll from a grocery store. Sadly, even the usually delicious chicken salad sandwich was extra salty this time. The least expensive tea service for Holiday tea is $100 plus tea service fee and tax. I expect the same delicious food we have enjoyed for the occasion not what we were served. Bring back the old menu. Everyone in our party was severely disappointed and if this menu remains we will be looking for another team service not only for Holiday tea but for our other afternoon teas throughout the year. Also, do NOT change the tea pots. Stop messing with a good thing and cheapening an expensive experience. I will say the service is impeccable and we love the team at the tea room. Just fix the food!

reviews.text:

We did not order the Thanksgiving dinner meal, we ordered the filet mignon Oscar, and the porterhouse steak. They were both excellent and they were served a la carte.
We both ordered specialty cocktails off of the drink menu and I do not recommend either of them LOL.
There is an incredible patio outside unfortunately it was not open. This is worthwhile to go and get anything here just to go out on the patio and experience The View. Our service took a very very long time. We were ignored for at least 5 minutes before we even made eye contact with any server.
As I said, check it out for the view you might want to eat ahead of time unless you want to pay about $350.

reviews.text: A loud, dated, marginally maintained property.  I get here and the check in and valet is like a casino.  They misplace the car for awhile and then have to find it again because I had to drive to my room instead.  The property is clearly dated, smells like the 1980s, and has VERY SMALL and uninteresting rooms for $1000 per nights.  The rooms, in fact, are not one single amenity better than the $140/night Hilton airport hotel.  For a huge resort like this, unbelievably, the outsource their laundry meaning it takes days to return to you.   They host some kind of rock concerts on their property because loud music was thumping on my window until late in the evening.  The open spaces felt like an apartment complex with screaming kids and sports, OK, cool, but the environment is anything but relaxing.   My "casita" has an outdoor space which is shared by others neighboring me and not cleaned up a bit from the last guests who left cigarette butts drowned in a cup of beer or something on the ground in plain sight.

reviews.text: I have been coming to the Phoenician for several years. I have never had an experience like I did tonight. I pulled up to the hotel and there was a man there to valet the cars. The Phoenician always has someone to valet your car. The man that was valeting for the evening  just stood outside the booth and looked at me. I waited patiently because I assumed that he was waiting for another valet person to come. After five minutes passed, he walked toward the passenger side, I was preparing to roll down the window and before getting to the car, he turned around and went in the back of the valet station. He stayed in the back of the valet station until another car pulled up. He immediately came out and proceeded to help the lady get out of her vehicle. I got out of my car once I realized that I was actually overlooked, disregarded and not acknowledged. I asked him why he didn’t come to my car and he lied and said I wouldn’t open the car for him. I spoke to the manager and he told me that he will take my keys to the same man that refused to take my keys initially. He apologized and appeared  to be unsure how to handle the situation. He asked me if I wanted a drink. I told him that what I want is for the tape to be viewed and for him to reprimand the valet guy. I don’t want this to happen to anyone else. I am a women of color and I am hoping that this was not done for that reason.

reviews.text:
The facility and rooms were in amazing condition. It felt brand new. The resort is beautiful and I would recommend it for a couple. Unfortunately we went with children. We were under the impression it would be good for small kids because of the splash pad and kids center. This was not the case. The resort is large and if you are not in the building close to the lobby, the pool is a long walk away. For a couple this wouldn't be a problem but when you have a stroller and pool stuff, it is a pain. The pool is large but has zero shade. Once you are in the pool, you are cooking. No canopy or structures to provide shade over any sections of the pool. Once again, fine for adults but not children.

The staff was disappointing as well. It didn't feel like a luxury service at all. Any questions seemed to have vague answers and no one was really that helpful. We booked a crib and confirmed during check in but it was never brought to our room until I requested a third time the next day. Another thing, I know this next one sounds very petty but how do you not have iced coffee at the pool restaurant? We were brought hot coffee over ice which just melted. Just a pet peeve lol.
We did have a valet who gave my son and I a golf cart ride around the property. My son loves golf carts and this was the best service we had the whole trip.

Another thing that was not mentioned was that the parking garage cost over 20 bucks a day. How is this not included or mentioned at check in? I would have just valeted for 2 bucks more a day. Also the TV didn't have many channels (once again we had kids with us). I was excited to see a kids package but realized they charged for it. It's just tacky when a place has everything being an extra charge.

The food was mediocre and waaaay over priced. This is normal for a resort but the food just all felt dated and wasn't that good.

Overall this would be fun for a couple or a golf trip. Just not for kids.

We have stayed at the Gainey Ranch resort and that was much much better for kids.

reviews.text:
UPDATE: You can see below that the Public Relations Director, from the hotel, assured me that my concerns would be addressed.

Well, its been over a month and I still haven't heard anything. Leaving me no choice but to conclude that she was just blowing smoke with her well practiced corporate response.

Is this non-response what is done to other people after givng assurances? Are you figuring that they'll blow off steam and then go away?

As I've now been ignored by the assigned rep, GM and Public Relatons Director, this is clearly a systemic problem.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
I tried to book through the group site as directed, without any luck. I called the rep assigned and it took multiple calls and emails to him, as well as a message for the GM, to get a response. One interesting point to note is that the GM never contacted me. Additional, 2 miscellaneous charges, that I was not told about, for portage and room cleaning, were added to my final bill. I never used portage services. When I contacted the rep to dispute them, he indicated that they were disclosed on the booking site. Well, as mentioned, I booked with him directly, so I didn't get a chance to see them on the site. This was brought to his attention by email and it's been a month or so and he is now ignoring this fact.
I'm curious to see how quickly and deftly the customer relation person, who seems to respond to reviews, responds to this one and spins it while showing false empathy and understanding with my dissatisfaction.

reviews.text: Hotel is pretty, waitstaff is nice, grounds and facilities are top notch and food is excellent.  However, the hotel did not seem to have a grasp of customer service. First, our room was not ready for 4PM check-in. After waiting 1.25 hrs. it was ready and we rec'd a $100 credit.  Mini-bar was completely empty upon arrival. Asked Concierge to arrange tennis during my stay and they handed me a sticky note with the tennis center's extension and told me to call myself and arrange it. Valet ($38/nite) had no charger available for at the main building for our Tesla. We were told we could drive across the resort ourselves to find one in another location. No chairs available in pool area except for the 30 that were available in the "Reserved Area" where they charge $50 per chair and a $50 drink min.  Made call to tennis pro shop. No one picked up and it went to voicemail. I left messages and no one returned my call. No water available in lobby, nor coffee in the morning. At $1000 per night I expected more. We didn't even get a chocolate on our pillow or water on our nightstand. Honestly, I've gotten better treatment at far less expensive hotels.  When I want to splurge again, I will spend my money elsewhere.

Our experience was disappointing. Our room, though spacious and clean did not just lack a vuew .. but was a view of the roof. I could excuse this.... But our experience pool aide was also lacking. No lifeguards were on duty, nor was there any circulating wait staff to bring a beverage or to order food from. The children's splash pad area was not heated, and the slide was closed. reviews.text: My wife, Lora, and I have stayed at many a fine hotel, and as Titanium members with Marriott, have grown accustomed to excellent customer service, but nothing has been as exceptional as our latest stay at the Phoenician in Arizona. From the moment we entered the resort, where we were warmly greeted by Eddie and Ryan at the front desk, who gave us a complimentary room upgrade, to the day we departed, when Charlotte in Food & Beverage gave us a complimentary fruit platter, the experience has been nothing short of exceptional. During our stay, when our flight was cancelled, Haley, a Front Desk Manager, and Jonathan, a Front Desk Agent, were kind and considerate, helping us negotiate another night, complete with a late checkout, for which we are grateful. Of course, the grounds of the resort are lovely, and the pools are amazing, but the best part of our wonderful stay has clearly been the people we had the pleasure of engaging with, so thank you to everyone at the Phoenician, you made Lora's and my 10 year anniversary exceptional, and we look forward to staying at your beautiful property again soon.

reviews.text:
Probably my favorite hotel! I've stayed here several times in the winter and summer. Was recently here in June 2020. Pretty busy for summer but I think everyone wanted to get out and travel with COVID pretty much gone. The hotels location is amazing.

Amazing views from the rooms and of course the pools! The pools here are so nice, even if it is 115 out. Most importantly, I LOVE that they are open 24/7. Going for a swim at midnight when no one is around and the sun is not glaring down is perfect. Not many hotels I've been to have this unfortunately. The slide is really fun. Yes, I was the only adult on it that day haha.

My only negative with my last stay was the house keeping. We stayed for almost a week and they never replaced towels or toiletries like shampoo. We had to call room service who was very quick at bringing it but shouldn't have to do that.

Other than that, it's an amazing resort. The cactus garden is amazing to see with Camelback Mountain right behind. Looking forward to come back soon.

reviews.text:
My wife, 6-month-old son and I stayed here over the past weekend. There are two of the residence units that are on top of each other, 7703 and 7704 with 7703 being on the ground level. We were unfortunately in 7703 for a 3-night stay and while the place is fantastic, you can hear EVERYTHING that's going on upstairs in 7704. We were just astonished at the level of noise that normal activity could make. Footsteps, talking, doors closing and opening, toilets flushing all sounded like this was happening in our own unit. This is something that I might expect from a cheap motel, but certainly not at a place like this especially given the amount of money we paid to stay there.

After the first night, we asked to be moved but they said the people upstairs were checking out and it wasn't booked for the next two nights but someone definitely checked in that afternoon. So, the normal activity upstairs continued to wake up our son during naps and at night meaning we had a very cranky 6-month-old the whole time we were there.

Other than that, everything was great. But if you check-in and they tell you that you are in 7703 of the Residences, buckle up, or ask to be in a different unit.

reviews.text: I am only giving them a one star because of the grounds and.lounge area. This has taken me a while to write this review because this is something that I normally do not do. We came here Christmas Eve to have a wonderful Christmas memory which became the opposite. To start the wait staff was horrible you could tell our waiter did not want to be there. My husband came out the bathroom and heard him saying that he got called in was not suppose to be there and did not want to be. We ordered our food the bus people brought it out cold. We did not see our waiter until we asked to see management which took 15 minutes to arrive. We complained to a young assistant manager and then finally our waiter that could have cared less. We went here because of the good reviews and to have a wonderful dinner with our daughter from out of town. We left hungry and angry luckily we didn’t have to pay for a thing if we would have then they would have seen a pretty angry person. reviews.text: We were to stay at this hotel for a NYE wedding. Three days prior to our arrival, our flight to PHX had been changed a few times and we could not be guaranteed an arrival. This was due to the airline's lack of crews due to COVID. We decided to cancel our trip as we had to connect coming and going. My wife, who made the reservation and is a LIFETIME Marriott TITANIUM member, had called the hotel after her credit card was charged with a one-day room charge. The hotel said that their cancellation policy was a 7-day notice, not the normal cancellation policy Marriott has and was not going to waive the charge no matter what the circumstances were. She called the Marriott help desk and they referred her back to the hotel for a "review". Today we received the notice that the hotel was not going to credit her the room charge. But they were nice enough to wish us a "Pleasant New Years and hope to see us soon". We HIGHLY recommend that you exercise caution when reserving a room at this resort DUE TO ITS UNFORGIVING RESERVATION AND CANCELLATION POLICY!

reviews.text:
Definitely not a 5* experience - more of a 4* experience.

- Had to queue up for about 30 mins to check in as they only had one person at the check in desk.

- Ordered a golf cart to take me to the spa - I had to wait 30 mins to be returned back to the main lobby by the golf cart.

They are clearly understaffed.

- The rooms are very very meh - the mountain view king room was not all that at all - the view was a bit suffocating its exactly like the picture the mountain is really close up its not like a view the mountains from afar kind of vibe. Omni is 100000000% nicer.

- The service at the bar was very poor. The bar staff don't come back to you to take your order, you have to keep trying to get their attention. Our wings came out cold. They forgot our order at one point and we had to remind them of what we ordered - they comped those dishes but definitely not a 5* experience.

The attention to detail was not there as you'd expect from a high end hotel that cost $800 for one night stay.

The view is beautiful from the bar area & the hotel its self is very pretty and scenic - but I wouldn't stay again. I'd 100% recommend going to the omni instead.

P.S. I did have afternoon tea here too at a different date which was fun but I'm British and the sandwiches weren't up to par.

reviews.text:
No stay is without issues but based on overall experience, I decided to give this resort a 4 ⭐️
PROS: Room was clean and big. Beautiful property with great service, nice pools, high quality food and service.
High Tea experience: Good experience but overpriced ($100 per person for 3 course after gratuity and tax)
Mowry and Cotton restaurant: We went to M and C during our stay to eat breakfast and dinner and feel that it’s of high quality in terms of food and service with nice views of the pool. Especially at night the blue light reflecting the pool was amazing.
Thirsty Camel bar: Great bar with nice outside seating area and 🔥 pits. Great drinks and service and live music.
CONS:
-CheckIn experience was not great, things were not explained clearly, for e.g I opted for self parking but no one explained that I could use my room key for in and out from the Self parking. I was paying every time using credit card every time I went in and out. Once I talked to the front desk, they were kind to waive the $23 per day charge they were going to charge me.
-On-site activities: Very few activities for kids or Christmas related events. We visited and attended the Fairmont Princess (a different resort in Scottsdale not associated with Marriott) Resort Christmas lights and ride experience ($72 for 4 with self parking included) and were blown away by the light and kids rides etc. Wish this resort had some nice Christmas lights and more activities for kids. If I had to book around Christmas, I would have booked Fairmont Princess resort just to have access to the Christmas light experience.
-Gym: Far from the property; have to use a golf cart to go there for bike rentals and use.
-Spa: We couldn’t get appointment because it was booked so can’t share the experience however feel it was overpriced

reviews.text:
I checked in for a four night stay last Thursday 11/15, after flying in from San Antonio, Texas. I booked a stay two months in advance for a one bedroom, executive suite, with a balcony with a resort view. What was supposed to be a nice luxurious stay in an amazing room, to enjoy room service and champagne for my birthday turned in to a total disappointment! The room we were given had zero view. It was a horrible room that faced on all sides the adjacent buildings. No trees, no grass, no garden, no camelback mountain, no saguaro, no pool…concrete buildings! I didn’t book this stay to be in a concrete jungle. The room wasn’t cleaned to my standards, dirty fridge, etc. Lack of decor, very underwhelming. I am not totally convinced they don’t ever use this room for guests due to its condition.

Management repeatedly told me that all rooms were booked solid and they could offer me a measly $400 resort credit for food and beverage. After two nights they put us in the room I assume should have been ours to begin with. After spending $4k for a four night stay at a so called five star hotel, we were taken advantage of and screwed over by management and this hotel. Not a pleasant or positive experience.
reviews.author: Stephanie Perez

reviews.text: I received a gift card for $200. The last 19 months with the pandemic we have not spent time traveling or at resorts.  When I called about using my $200 gift card I was told it expired and there was nothing that could be done.  I thought for sure an establishment like the Phoenician was making exceptions considering the pandemic and limited services,  travel,  and all health recommendations. I asked that the representative forward me to a manager so I could explain.  I was within a month of the expiration date.  It did it take Denise, Director of Public Relations and Marketing,  several days,  if not a week to return my call,  but she was listening when she finally did call so I didn't mind.  She asked that I send a picture because gift cards do not expire.  Great,  I didn't mind the delay so much,  however she emailed me shortly after receiving the photo and said this card does expire and they were not making any exceptions  due to pandemic, travel limitations,  and health recommendations. SHE STATED THE CARD WAS "OUT OF CIRCULATION FOR YEARS".  IT WAS JUST EXPIRED A FEW DAYS, NOT YEARS.  DO NOT BUY A GIFT CARD FROM THE PHOENICIAN.  I can't bring myself to tell my husband it was wasted money.

reviews.text:
With ~400 Bonvoy nights and stays at over a half dozen properties in the luxury collection portfolio, this by far the worst property and experience. I would avoid and suggest elsewhere should you stay in Scottsdale (you can get much better for far less). Specifically,
- Am lifetime gold elite
- Checked in on the app as early as available - apprx 24 hrs before arrival
- Had booked and reconfirmed King room
- Requested early check in

When I arrived not only was there no early check-in (which understand it’s only if available) but then they also put us in a room with two queens, see attached photo for our “view”. This hotel’s avg. rate is somewhere around $800 I believe. There was tremendous turnover the day we checked in so I am certain they could’ve found us a king sized room or even a better view (not to mention try for an upgrade, again, part of gold status, but of course also only if available). They didn’t even try. Hospitality is dead

Went to the restaurant while waiting for the room to be ready. Couldn’t even get any server to grab a second beer. I get that everyone is short staffed and trying, but again, you’re paying for “luxury” and this ain’t it.

reviews.text: I recently stayed at The Phoenician Resort last month. Upon my arrival at the valet I was asked if I wanted to leave my golf club set with them and they would hold for me in a storage room and thought that was convenient so I did. During my 5 day stay I did not end up golfing afterall so I never used or asked for my clubs until the day I checked out. When I was given my golf club set back I was missing 3 clubs and my bag was completely rearranged almost as if someone messed with it or used it. I was told I had to file an incident report with their insurance company which I did that has been going on over a month now only to be told that unfortunately they cannot do anything regarding my missing items. Throughout this time I heard from their insurance adjuster 3 times and that is after countless calls and emails I had to make and send over regarding my claim. After reading multiple reviews in scenarios such as mine it seems nothing is ever done nor resolved from either their insurance company or the resort. I had to go through security, insurance and a lot of back and forth with several people only to be told that nothing can be done anyway. Very unpleasant experience during my stay.
reviews.author: Diego M

reviews.text: The property is stunning. I stayed in a deluxe King room and it was perfect for me. Although the spa and steakhouse were all booked up, I still enjoyed my time using the other amenities.

reviews.author: Sean Campbell

reviews.text: Love their "casitas" super clean!  Def keeps us coming back every year.
reviews.author: Eve

reviews.text: The property is nice and well maintained on the outside. Our room had the following issues: 1st, we ordered a room with a poolside view. That's what we paid for. We were told it was not available when we checked in because they overbooked. So we were given another room with a golf course view. When we got to the room the only view we had was a loading dock and some forklifts. And they charged us extra for moving us to another room. 2nd, there was a broken glass on the floor and glass shards in the doorway and bathroom. The sink was dirty and drained very slowly. The cleaning staff left their cleaning materials in the room. At 2pm we finally got our room cleaned. They replaced the shower towels only. No hand towels, no face cloths. We called several times to ask for these items to be returned to our room. We never got them. The service was slow but the service team was nice once you got their attention. The hotel has no shuttle service to take you any where. You have to use Uber or Lyft. The concierge station could not answer a single question for us. They couldn't help get us towels either. And finally the valet team brings us the wrong car causing us to wait even longer to get out of there. No, it was not very busy. It's sad that being the person on crutches standing there waiting for our car that we had to wait longer than any other guest. The food was pricey but very good. Drinks were very good. The rest of the service was no better than a Holiday Inn. Save your money, this place is over rated. Won't be returning.
reviews.author: Ken Crawford

reviews.text: Beautiful, well maintained resort. Upon arrival, concierge informed us the spa was not available the entire duration of our stay. Instead of coming up with other suggestions we were given the cold shoulder. Also given the ultimatum of being kicked out of the pool or throw away a fruit cup purchased at the resort Marketplace… Absolutely shocked to see two additional invoices after checkout for “daily resort fees” amounting to another $50/ day. Not up front about this at all and feel like our credit card is an open check book that random fees keep popping up on since leaving. Overall staff experience was “we can help you have a great time but it will cost you $$$”. Not trying to sound cheap by any means but our expectations were to relax and have a good time. It was difficult to do this without shelling money out left and right to the resort we already booked and paid for.
reviews.author: hayden hanna

reviews.text: Beautiful resort at the base of Camelback. Lots of pools, good dining and attentive staff. Don’t miss the tea service. Close to Old Town.

reviews.text: It was a very nice birthday gift from my husband. On Open Table the dress stated Formal Attire. There were many guests in shorts, t-shirts, swimwear cover-ups. I had on dress pants and a blouse before we left for our reservation.  I  changed to a dress before we left in respect to their attire statement. Once we arrived to our reservation, I realized I didn't need to worry that I was under dressed and could have worn my dress pants  and blouse and my new purse, which I was keeping for a special occasion. ☺
reviews.author: Catherine Lopez

reviews.text: Visited for a business conference. Left with a flurry of activities under our belt: swimming, pickle ball, golf, weights, eating and more! Thank f you’re in Scottsdale, this is the place!
reviews.author: Mishan Andre

reviews.text: Incredible place, beautiful gardens

reviews.text: Great resort in Scottsdale, Arizona.  The Phoenician is large and has several pools, golf course, restaurants and spa. Great views of the mountain.

reviews.text: What a beautiful resort! I stayed here for business, it was comfortable, enjoyable and so spacious! My husband joined me the last couple of nights and it was romantic and we had so much fun at the pool too! The staff was so kind and friendly, I can't wait to come back!

reviews.text: Such a nice place.  Scones with clotted cream was great.  Tea flavors are plentiful and you can get different types of tea throughout your time.  We sipped tea, enjoyed life and pretended we were English for a couple hours while taking in the beautiful resort.  Pricey, but worth doing if you like drinking tea.

reviews.text: Great service.
reviews.author: James Musselman

reviews.text:
Me and my wife had an amazing time at the Phoenician. Rooms were gorgeous and clean with amazing views. Great sunrises every morning, it was relaxing and calm. It is a family resort but there’s 3 pools so you can choose which pool you want to be whether it’s the adults only or the family one. Food was amazing as well. Try all the restaurants , you won’t be disappointed.

The names of the ones who helped us and were so kind were
Marissa - pool side
Nicole - pool side
Barbara’s- pool side

Rita - fitness club

Fransisca - houskeeeping

Kevin - bellboy

Kaylie- front desk

-I wish I remember the girl who waited on us at the afternoon tea but I can’t- she was amazing.

The only reason I’m giving this 4 stars is because of Luis M. At the mowry and cotton restaurant. I’m not sure if it’s cause we decided to eat outside and he hated that he had to walk to us. But he was not a good waiter. He was impatient and not kind. The guy pouring the water gave us more attention than Luis did. By the end of it he said “I’m just gonna be straightforward , have a good stay”
I’m not even sure what that means lol but it was our first night there , so kind of annoying to be treated so poorly just cause of where we decided to sit.

**also I want to add. Because I’m deeply offended by this persons review saying he had covid and went anyways cause they wouldn’t refund. First off. You can dispute charges on your credit card. Second off. Don’t say the hotel doesn’t care. They have contracts and stipulations when you purchase. And if you buy 3rd party you will have a harder time getting your money back. Buy from Marriott directly. Spend the few extra bucks, read the details and fine print and you will be fine. And stay home if you have covid**
reviews.author: Syah Johan

reviews.text: Came to the spa for our anniversary for our first time and it was absolutely perfect! The guest attendants to the therapist it was an absolute pleasure.
reviews.author: Ivory Stafford

reviews.text: Went to dinner at J & G Steakhouse and checked out the resort. Absolutely beautiful, and we LOVED the restaurant.
reviews.author: Joshua Sittig

reviews.text: Well just to let people know my boyfriend loved it, I wasn't there .
reviews.author: Diane Lentz

reviews.text: Upscale resort with amazing service. The pools are excellent. The main pool has a water-park quality slide and a kids area with different places to splash around and get wet in case the little ones can't swim yet. Also nearby a wading pool. On the second level they have an adults only pool for a more relaxed atmosphere. Finally on the lower level nearest the spa is the Mother of Pearl pool ,which I Iearned ,was actually inlaid with mother of pearl tile when it was built in the 1920's. The staff is excellent!! Very attentive and accommodating. One can reserve a cabana or order meal on their smart phone and truly get the "full service". . money well spent.
reviews.author: Alan Digan

reviews.text:
The property is gorgeous, albeit alittle tattered. Overall, every staff member I encountered was helpful, friendly and seemed to enjoy their job. Omar and Sydney out by the pool were very attentive and I was able to take some time to relax by the pool.

My day started with room service and breakfast on the patio looking at Camelback. Unfortunately, the table cloth had 2 holes in it, one someone had attempted to repair with the wrong color thread. Really, replace tattered tablecloths.

The afternoon at the pool, resulted in returning 2 towels that had holes in them for different ones. Took a few to find towels that weren't frayed.

I expect all aspects of the luxury collection to be first class, not just the staff. Looks to be like the linens need to be replaced.

The devil is in the details, and its the little things that make the difference.
reviews.author: Pam Bailey

reviews.text: I had a friend who stayed here this past summer and had a bag of clothes stolen out of her room by the cleaning lady’s , no apologies from staff and the way my friend was treated was downright disgusting as if she was the criminal. It’s been 1 month later and she’s still dealing with dissatisfied customer service  and not one employee has offered her any type of complimentary kindness from the Marriott. Corporate was called etc, I live in Scottsdale and I referred these guests there to be treated like this?! , this was nothing but a mere embarrassment and I will and have told anyone I come in contract with as well as employees at the hospital to steer clear of this place , I will never refer ever again another one of my guests  who comes into town to this place. This all could of been resolved had the phonecian had just made my friend feel as if they cared.

reviews.text: This is how much the Phoenician cares about 1. its customers, 2. its employees. I have a reservation for the 13-15th however on the 9th I tested positive for covid as did my wife. I tried to cancel my reservation and provided documentation and as you see they refuse and will not refund my money. They stated I can reschedule, I'm about to miss 14 days of work, how could I possibly request more time? With that being said, unfortunately I refuse to lose $940 so I WILL be there this Friday, I will dine in the restaurant I will use the attractions of the resort including the bar and pool. No I am not proud of it, but I will not throw away my mortgage. If I could give them 0 stars I would and I will look into the better business bureau. Avoid this place the weekend of the 13th and at least a week after.

reviews.text: Just stunning and excellent!
reviews.author: lloyd sample

reviews.text:
For years I have heard of this property from friends and clients that have been going for years. The property is large and spread out, but access is very easy with golf carts that arrive when you request them.
The spa is world renowned and "huge." The vibe is special and intended for a full day experience. The Canyon Suites with a spa focus vacation would not disappoint anyone wanting a special disconnect of pampering.
Many restaurants to choose from, we tried The Tavern and Mowry & Cotton. There was retail sprinkled in as well, R&R is a fun store.
The multiple pools were a highlight. High touch of ice water by the pool staff was very appreciated.
Joanna Paulsel was a joy and her long history with the property put an impressive cap on the reputation and experience on my visit. There are many long time employees which says a lot for the owners and management.
reviews.author: cyndi becker

reviews.text:
My fiancé and I have been visiting the Phoenician regularly for a couple of years and every time we visit, we are provided with the most impeccable service by Deano at the main bar.
He greets us warmly, provides entertaining conversation and is always attentive in serving us.
In fact, the last time we visited the resort, my fiancé proposed, and Deano played a part in ensuring it all went smoothly!
Deano goes above and beyond to ensure that we always feel well looked after and it never goes unnoticed. We look forward to visiting again and seeing Deano on our next trip.
reviews.author: Eli G

reviews.text: I’ve been blessed to have stayed at some of the finest hotels in the world and I can say without hesitation that The Phoenician Hotel and Resort in Scottsdale, AZ is superb. Understated elegance, astonishing spa, beautiful architecture and setting, excellent cuisine, incredible array of classy pools and sophisticated service makes this my favorite Scottsdale Resort. Off season, on, or in between, they’ll make your stay here incredibly memorable.
reviews.author: Steve Sulkin

reviews.text: Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Nathan Rademaker

reviews.text: Our host Daphne was amazing ! She helped us find a spot by one of the amazing pools on our first day and then remembered us for the rest of our stay. Like the rest of the staff we met, she was friendly, helpful and clearly loves what she does, which says a lot about the Phoenician. Beautiful spot on the mountain, and left feeling incredibly rested and restored. Thanks !
reviews.author: Jo-Anne Mckee

reviews.text:
Love the Phoenician, have always looked at it as a premier hotel. We were excited to see all the new renovations so booked staycation this past weekend. The property is gorgeous, the customer service however was extremely disappointing.
-The Netflix connection is incredibly cumbersome, took over an hour to figure out. Finally connected and then weak wifi disconnected repeatedly.
-Remote control had to be changed out
-found someone else reading glasses in room, which made us question how well rooms getting cleaned?
-Moury & Cotton Rest. Front desk staff (Isaiah) was so rude my 10 year old asked me why he was working there. I asked to talk to mgr and he never sent one over?
-Gift shops have min. you have to spend to charge to room. I have never seen this before? They said it was because of Covid?
-They only have 2 people working the operator station, I spend 15 min on hold. Was so frustrated I had to leave 5 kids and walk to front desk to get issue taken care of?

If you are going for a couples get away it would be great, but if you are looking to bring kids you will leave frustrated. For us, doesn't matter how many millions you spend to make property great again if staff is rude, and understaffed.

There are so many great resorts in AZ, this one still has a long way to go to becoming premier hotel again.
reviews.author: Chad Archibeck

reviews.text: My husband and I went for our anniversary and had a fantastic time! We got there a little early but the front desk agent, Kaylee, was friendly and we were placed into a room immediately. We were happy (again, we were early) also, she was knowledgeable about activities available for us to try. The man at the athletic club was stand-out-helpful and friendly. Ana Laura at the Tavern was infectiously happy, and the craft beer tasting was ice cold! The room was comfortable, food and drinks delicious, and the little touches made it memorable. We were told Happy Anniversary with a wine and cheese plate delivered to our room, what a wonderful touch! We will definitely be back- such amazing and friendly service!
reviews.author: Shana Medlock

reviews.text: best hotel ever. Great and helpful staff. Clean rooms. Great pool, food, location, and everything imaginable. worth every dollar.
reviews.author: Grayson Baxter

reviews.text: My husband and I stayed here for our anniversary and we had such a wonderful time at the Phonecian Resort! We absolutely loved it! All of the staff are amazing! We had lunch at Mowry and Cotton and it was awesome! We made dinner reservations at J&G’s and it was so delicious and perfect because it was right in the hotel! So convenient! The little market was great for an on the go snack or breakfast. We enjoyed the our time at the pool with their refreshing daiquiri cocktails. The staff at the pool are so nice and helpful. We can’t wait to come back with our kids so they can enjoy the splash pad and the other kid activities. Thank you Phonecian!
reviews.author: kangeles27

reviews.text:
Went for a drink at the Thirsty Camel Lounge.
The policy is that you give your credit card ahead of getting your drinks. At the time to pay the check, the waiter informed me that they misplaced my card (it was given to another guest, who left with it).
The staff said they would work with security and find ways to retrieve my card. Despite the hotel telling me they would keep me informed everyday of the progress, I have not received any information and my card is still misplaced.
Of course, I just need to cancel my card and the various recurring payments I have on them and wait for a week to get a new one...but when you take someone credit card ahead of the transaction, you must take all measures to protect it. And when a mistake happens, at least you make your best to support your customer.
Watch out when you go there; you might be charged someone else lunch and lose your credit card.

reviews.text: We would not stay at hotel again.  Had to change rooms due to stains on couch and carpets.  Second room not much better.  Still stains on carpet, mold in shower, shower head leaked, dirty towels not picked up when clean ones delivered and vent in shower was dirty.  It was disgusting.  Will never stay again…money wasted.

reviews.text: We thoroughly enjoyed our time here at The Phoenician. It was one of the nicest resorts my husband and I have ever stayed in. Service was amazing. Amenities were all top notch. Everyone we met was so kind and went above and beyond to help us or to fulfill our requests the whole time we were here. They made the whole stay so convenient that we never had to want for anything. Whenever we are in the Scottsdale area, we will absolutely be staying here again!
reviews.author: Christine

reviews.text:
This review is not complete because of the word limit
First and foremost I want to start off by saying my partner and I were celebrating our anniversary and chose this “luxury resort” as a form of stay-cation to relax and enjoy our years of being together. For the money we spent for a single day and night at this resort I am EXTREMELY disappointed, and it truly all began from the moment we drove up to check-in. The valet was a mess, no one would even bother to help us with our bags or car so we ended up parking a distance away from the front desk and walking, with all of our things, to check in. So obviously irritated already, it was no shocker that we were told our room wasn’t ready and we could give our bags to some bell hops if we wanted to while we waited. I informed the man who was checking us in, Corey I believe (?), that we had a treatment at the spa that day and wanted to wait and relax there until we were able to go to our room. He assured us that wouldn’t be a problem and we could give our bags and car to the valet and they would shuttle us to the spa. HA! When we told this to the valet they informed us that it “actually will be quite a while before anyone can shuttle us” so we’re better off driving ourselves to the parking garage by the spa. Of course, who’s surprised at this point. Also I told the man checking us in that it was our anniversary and if it was possible we would love a cooler and champagne glasses available in our room when it was ready. All we had asked for was two glasses and some ice and you would’ve sworn we were asking for the entire complex on a silver platter by the way he looked at us. He flat out denied us and told us we can call room service once we were admitted to our room if we still wanted that - no congratulations, nothing. Thanks, five star service indeed I guess. So my partner and I drive ourselves down to the spa, which was the single enjoyable part of the day. I truly do not have anything negative to say about the spa or the staff. They were incredibly accommodating and we immensely enjoyed not only our couples massage, but the cabana we rented on the rooftop that day…. And then our nightmare began again. When we left the front desk from checking in we were told we would receive a call that our room was ready, at the latest 4 pm…. It was 5:30 when we left the spa and we hadn’t received a call or anything. also I should say that the spa staff repeatedly asked us for our room number and it was pretty embarrassing to have to say we had no idea because, you guessed it, no one had told us a thing about our room or when it would be ready! So we leave at 5:30, drive ourselves back to the front desk, where once again not a single person asks to help us with our car so, once again, we park a distance away and walk to the front (same old song and dance huh). We’re finally handed our keys and told where the room is. And guess where it is, right. Next. To the spa. Where we just came from…. So how many unnecessary trips did we take just to drive ourselves right back to where we had came from. Oh and can I add that no bell hop dropped our bags at our room for us, they just handed them to us from where they were being stored and we were of course on our own again. So naturally we decide to dine away from this egregious, disappointing resort. Best part of the evening truly. We return around 9 and start winding down from the day. Around 11 pm, our neighbors decide it’s a FANTASTIC idea to invite all six of their friends they’re visiting the resort with out onto their balcony which is directly next to ours with no walls between. We could hear (and smell) EVERYTHING. They were screaming until 1 am. We called the front desk TWICE to complain and they assured us they were sending security to handle it. HA, for a second time! Trust me, we would’ve known if security had bothered to knock on their door because we could hear every. Single. Word. They were saying and I think I would know if one of them had
reviews.author: Rachel Carroll

reviews.text: My stay was great as always, but today I am writing about Andrew.  I had been trying to reach a department for over a week with no success.  Andrew explained why I hadn't gotten a response and immediately got the information to get this resolved.  Great attitude and work ethic.  Work ethic is hard to find today so kudo's to you Andrew.  Keep up the great work!
reviews.author: BigDaddyK 1275

reviews.text: We had a fairly mixed experience at The Phoenician during our 9-night stay. The hotel property is very nice and looks beautiful. Pools are nice also, except way too warm. I would think a hotel of this caliber can afford some pool cooling equipment as getting into a 95 degree pool is not pleasant when it is 115 degreed outside. Service by the pool was pretty good though. Rooms are fine, nothing special, but our towels were dirty. Calling for help/front desk/service required a 5 min wait on hold every single time. Would you expect this from a 5-star hotel? Front desk service is also terrible, there was always a long line and the people at the front desk did not appear to have much interest in helping anyone. For example, when checking in, I was told my room was not ready, no other rooms were available and I just had to wait. Yet, literally 5 min later a room was given to another person we knew (same room type as ours, same length stay). So how was no room available when I was checking in and miraculously appeared 5 min later??? My room keys stopped working one day (after the front deck people tried to enable them to work in the parking garage) and I had to stand in line for 20 min to have their mistake fixed which made us late for a tour. Parking garage is too small and tight and was supposed to work with my room key (which only actually worked twice and was broken the rest of the times). Food options are also very limited on property and prices are outrageous. We ordered breakfast for 4 people once and it cost $150 (for two orders of eggs, one order of pancakes and one order of waffles, with two orange juices and one coffee). Overall, not a completely horrible stay, but I would not return to this hotel (and I am a Bonvoy Lifetime Platinum member).
reviews.author: Boris Nemirov

reviews.text: I had problems trying to book a stay there, haven't even stayed there yet.  The first time I called I got cut off because I was on hold so long, second time I called same thing, so I called later then 3rd time I called the gentleman told me that there beds were made of feather when I told him that I was allergic he said then I guess you would have a problem staying here. I called Marriott because I thought that was weird and they checked into it and it wasn't true just the pillows and duvet had feathers, so I called back to try again and make a reservation.  I asked if we could get a room by the entrance and restaurants because my husband has a leg injury and cannot walk far with his cane and she said that did not have a room close to the entrance so she put us in a casitas room furthest away from the lobby and said she cannot guarantee anything, ask for a feather free bed due to allergies said she would put it down a request it but can't guarantee it.  After I hung up I realized this doesn't seem like good customer service practices so I called back to talk to a manager, they took a message after listening to my long story and said someone would call me back to help me with this situation and it has been 3 days and nobody has called me back.  I just cancelled my reservations. Terrible customer service!

The Garden, presenting the flora of the desert is simply amazing. Restaurants and bars to delight you at any time. The Spa and pools to relax you when needed.  Loved it! Montserrat

We had the most exceptional stay! First and foremost, the resort is beautiful and clean. The entire grounds is beautifully unkept.
We got to the hotel way earlier then check in and we were able to get a room. The receptionist at check in was so kind, friendly and helpful! We also got a later check out which was so nice.

The room was spacious, clean and had a very comfortable bed!

The pools were great! The workers who helped set up your chairs were phenomenal! You didn’t even have to ask them for help. They just did it.
The servers were all so great, specifically Berkley who we had two of the days. She went out of her way to provide the best service and experience. She made us dinner reservations and even found us our drink that was out at the bar.

Food was so great! There wasn’t a bad meal that we had. My husband said the steak house had the best steak he’d ever had.
The bar in the main lobby was great. Don was amazing!

There isn’t one bad thing I could say about our stay. We will be back and we plan to bring our kids!

When our room was made up it was done so haphazardly that look like my children made the bed. Anytime we sat by the pool we had to wait forever to get anyone to come and help us. At the restaurants the servers had to be asked at least three times to get some thing as simple as a glass of ice. On check out day I called and called the bell desk, the front desk, and the operator and got no answer for at least 30 minutes. I even called from my cell phone the outside line to the hotel and did not get through. What a disappointment! At one time this was such a premier resort and the way that we were treated this time made me feel like I was at some unrated hotel.

reviews.text:
Review segment 1 of 4:

General: The food is excellent, but you'd be better off staying literally anywhere else and just visiting the restaurants. It's exorbitantly expensive, and they still charge you for something every time you turn around, and provide you the absolute bare minimum for a hotel stay (of any tier). The service would probably be great if they didn't overwork their employees and had more staff to take care of their guests. Oh, and don't think you can get in anywhere to eat or relax during your stay unless you've made reservations several days ahead of time. I have provided more detailed pros/cons below. You have been warned!

Negative:
-Room- My mother and I flew to AZ to aid in a family health issue, and because it was going to be a long and stressful visit, I thought I would treat my mother and myself to a stay at this luxurious resort (it was Mother's Day as well, after all). Because we would be spending all of our downtime during these 10 days at the resort, I wanted to make sure we had an absolutely spectacular view, as shown in the pictures on their website. Upon booking I emphasized this factor, and the concierge helped guide my room selection appropriately, although they recommended a follow up call before I flew out to verify the room selection. I called twice before arriving to verify, and each time was assured of the beautiful garden views we'd get to enjoy during our 10-day extended stay. I traveled for 16 hours to get there, and at the end of a long day, I arrived late in the evening for check in. Before even going to the room to get settled for the night, I again verified the room requirements with the concierge. He said he was unsure of the view of that room, but if we were unsatisfied with the space once we got there, he would happily move us. (This is laughable in retrospect). It took several minutes to get to our room, as it was the very last one at the end of the hotel, past many utility spaces and conference rooms. It was probably a storage space that was later converted to a room. The room was spacious, but seemed unfinished (some items in the room were still extremely dirty (spilled makeup, and a few unknown substances), there was a garbage bag still in the room, and the beds looked as though they'd merely been made, not newly cleaned). I was so exhausted after traveling so long that I was willing to let these issues go so I could get to sleep. But then we opened the draperies to assess our "beautiful view" that we'd be gazing at for the next 10 days: it was the gravel rooftop, huge metal exhaust vents for the hotel, and their loading dock where utility vehicles and delivery men frequented! It was so ludacris it seemed to be a cruel joke. The bellhop asked about where to put our luggage, and I felt awful making him wait, but the concierge insisted we call if there were any issues with the view, and this was too much to overlook. However, after being on hold for almost 10 minutes, I finally got through to the concierge, only to find out that moving us to another room would be IMPOSSIBLE as they had every. single. room. booked out for the next several days. And this was not at limited capacity due to Covid restrictions, this was every single room being taken up on the entire property! About halfway through our stay they'd have a room open up elsewhere on the property, but until then we were stuck. When we moved, we were glad to at least have a better view, but the second room was so cramped that you couldn't leave the room if either of the closets or the bathroom doors were open! Surely this is a fire hazard?! We also had an alarming cleanliness issue in the new room (the second day of our stay there we discovered someone had spilled popcorn in our room in the middle of the floor while we'd been out! There isn't even a microwave in the room, and this happened while we were gone during the day, so it was very alarming to find).

reviews.text:
I stayed at the resort from 03/18/21 - 03/23/21. I originally booked my stay through Orbitz. Despite paying for my stay 100% in advance months before our stay, at checkout, I was charged for my stay (+ incidentals) at checkout. I've called Orbitz and they provided me evidence that they paid Marriot for our stay and there is nothing they can do to assist further. I've spoken to Marriot corporate and they have acknowledged the problem. Apparently I'm not the only guest to experience this problem.

Despite regular assurances my money would be refunded, it's been almost 30 days (aka. a full credit card billing cycle) and I have yet to receive my refund.

I'm still waiting for my $5,126.06 to be refunded with no relief in sight.

The resort is beautiful, but their customer service, and sorry, their room service food quality, is worse than that of a Red Roof Inn. I wouldn't recommend staying here. I've never scene anyone so nonchalant and OK stealing $5,000.00 from a customer before.

I guess... never trust these people with a debit card - LOL!

This was a beautiful getaway backed up to camel back mountain where you can go on a nice hike. They have a gorgeous golf course, multiple swimming pools, adult pool and cabanas. Pools are open 24hrs. Room service is impeccable with a nice menu. There are shops in the hotel where you can buy designer sunglasses , swimsuits, and clothing . They have a world known bar that comes with the most exquisite drinks made by top bartenders.
It is also minutes from the airport and downtown Scottsdale.
There is much more to enjoy and I will leave it up to you to explore.
I would like to give a special thanks to the staff for making my wife and myself feel like royalty!
